manifest_declaration.title: Upper-tail p-values under an explicit null calibration
manifest_declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; current readiness is recorded separately.
manifest_declaration.statement:
Let $(S,\mathcal S,\{\mathbb P_\theta\}_{\theta\in\Theta})$ be a statistical model, let $\Theta_0\subseteq\Theta$ be a nonempty null set, and let $T:S\to\mathbb R$ be a statistic whose upper-tail sets are measurable. Fix an explicit calibration probability measure $Q_0$ on $(\mathbb R,\mathcal B(\mathbb R))$ for the statistic under the null procedure. For a simple null $\Theta_0=\{\theta_0\}$, the exact calibration is $Q_0=\mathbb P_{\theta_0}\circ T^{-1}$. For a composite null or an asymptotic analysis, $Q_0$ is supplied by the specified calibration procedure, whose nuisance-parameter treatment and approximation assumptions are part of the data.

For an observed datum $s\in S$, with the convention that larger $T$ values are more extreme, the upper-tail p-value is
$$p_0(s):=Q_0\bigl(\{t\in\mathbb R:t\ge T(s)\}\bigr).$$
It is a probability under the stated null calibration for a test statistic at least as extreme as the observed one. It is not a probability assigned to the null hypothesis conditional on the data; no probability distribution on $\Theta$ is supplied by this definition. The definition alone establishes neither type-I error control nor super-uniformity; any such validity claim requires a separate argument for the specified sampling model and calibration. A lower-tail or two-sided procedure must specify its own measurable extremeness set instead of using the displayed upper-tail convention.

manifest_declaration.statement: Fix a finite jet order $r$, maximum polynomial field degree $q$, engineering weight $D$, finite field-species list, coefficient field $\mathbb C$, and complex reductive affine algebraic group $G$ with the finite-dimensional rational action specified on the jet generators, including the declared spacetime-index symmetries. Let $W_D$ be the finite-dimensional space of all local polynomials of weight $D$ and degree at most $q$, before imposing $G$-invariance, and let $V_D=W_D^G$ be its invariant scalar subspace. An admitted raw relation space is a specified $G$-stable linear subspace $\widetilde R_D\leq W_D$, given by explicit linear identities among the chosen polynomials. Its invariant part is $R_D=\widetilde R_D\cap V_D$. Any action, boundary, or observable interpretation of the selected identities is extra mathematical data and must be stated with the result that verifies it.

manifest_declaration.title: Physical EFT operator data and power-counting contract
manifest_declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; finite-jet contract, exact quotient representatives, supplier scale conventions, sources, and current dependency interfaces recorded; readiness ready.
manifest_declaration.statement:
Use four-dimensional Minkowski space $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$, coordinates $x^0=ct$ and metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and natural units $c=\hbar=1$ for mass-dimension counting. A **physical EFT operator contract** is a record of the following selected model data; none of the selections is inferred from an operator's name.

Here an EFT is an adopted low-energy model whose local Lagrangian is organized by specified fields, symmetries, coefficients, and a finite retained order; this definition implies no ultraviolet completion or physical realization. First choose a finite set $I$ of field species. For each $i\in I$, specify a finite-dimensional complex graded space $\Phi_i=\Phi_i^{\bar 0}\oplus\Phi_i^{\bar 1}$, its bosonic or fermionic parity, its smooth field domain on $M$, any reality condition, and its assigned rational engineering weight $\Delta_i$. Even fields are smooth maps $M\to\Phi_i^{\bar 0}$; odd field components take values in a fixed Grassmann algebra with smooth coefficient functions. A spurion is a fixed, non-dynamical parameter assigned a representation and engineering weight, used to record a declared symmetry-breaking insertion. The proper orthochronous Lorentz group is $SO^+(1,3)=\{L\in GL_4(\mathbb R):L^T\eta L=\eta,\ \det L=1,\ L^0{}_0\ge1\}$; specify its finite-dimensional action on all spacetime indices and require each Lagrangian density to be a Lorentz scalar. State the full gauge and flavor actions on every field, index, and spurion. A flavor symmetry that is absent is recorded as trivial; an approximate or explicitly broken symmetry requires its breaking spurions and weights to be listed.

For a non-Abelian gauge sector, specify the compact real gauge group with its actual global form, smooth right principal bundle, admitted bundle sectors, unitary representations, and a smooth principal connection. The connection is a Lie-algebra-valued one-form reproducing fundamental vertical vectors and transforming by the adjoint action; its local curvature is $F_A=dA+\tfrac12[A\wedge A]$, and the covariant derivative in a representation $\rho$ is $D_\mu\psi=\partial_\mu\psi+\rho_*(A_\mu)\psi$. The field and connection data must include their regularity and spacetime and internal index representations. These formulas use the right-principal-bundle convention fixed by the supplied gauge-geometry definitions.

The local operator algebra uses a separate finite-dimensional rational representation of a complex reductive affine algebraic group $G_{\mathrm{alg}}$ on the finite jet generators. A contract must supply the maps and representations relating $G_{\mathrm{alg}}$ to the selected compact gauge group and flavor group. It must either verify, on each retained finite jet space, that the algebraic invariant subspace is exactly the intended physical invariant space, or label the quotient as a formal algebraic selection only. Compactness of a real gauge group alone does not identify its invariant polynomials with those of an algebraic complexification.

Choose nonnegative integer cutoffs $r$ and $q$, a coefficient field (here $\mathbb C$) and its conjugation data, and a finite rational maximum engineering dimension $D_{\max}$. With derivatives assigned weight one, the local field-jet definition supplies the supercommutative polynomial module $P_r=\operatorname{Sym}(J_{r,\bar 0}^*)\otimes\Lambda(J_{r,\bar 1}^*)$ and its fixed-weight subspaces. For each weight $D$, let $W_D$ be the finite raw polynomial space, $V_D=W_D^{G_{\mathrm{alg}}}$ its invariant scalar subspace, and $\widetilde R_D$ the explicitly declared $G_{\mathrm{alg}}$-stable linear relation subspace. The selected operator quotient is $\mathcal Q_D=V_D/(\widetilde R_D\cap V_D)$: it identifies exactly the declared relations and makes no completeness claim about all EFT redundancies. For each retained $D$, choose a vector-space basis of $\mathcal Q_D$ and one representative $\mathcal O_\alpha\in V_D$ of each basis class; write $\mathcal I_{\mathrm{op}}$ for the resulting finite set of representative labels and $\Delta_\alpha$ for the weight of $\mathcal O_\alpha$. The finite jet, field-degree, and dimension cutoffs give a finite-dimensional retained space, and the fixed-cutoff monomial set gives finitely many retained weights and representatives.

For each $\widetilde R_D$, record each generator as a polynomial or Fierz identity, a total divergence under compact-support or stated boundary conditions, or a leading-equation or field-redefinition relation tied to an explicit base action and retained order. An equation-of-motion entry records its variational derivative and field multiplier; a field-redefinition entry records the local map, its inverse through the retained order, and all induced higher-order terms. The quotient is a definition of the declared relation space; its existence alone does not establish action, off-shell Green-function, quantum-measure, or scattering equivalence.

Choose the canonical-dimension power-counting scheme, coefficient truncation, and a nonnegative integer loop order $L_{\max}$. The formal loop label $\zeta$ is dimensionless bookkeeping and is not a convergence claim. If $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}>0$ is the coefficient-suppression scale, the retained local Lagrangian has the convention

$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{tr}}=\sum_{\substack{\alpha\in\mathcal I_{\mathrm{op}}\\\Delta_\alpha\le D_{\max}}}\sum_{\ell=0}^{L_{\max}}\zeta^\ell C_{\alpha,\ell}(\mu_W)\frac{\mathcal O_\alpha}{\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}^{\Delta_\alpha-4}},$$

where each $\mathcal O_\alpha$ has engineering weight $\Delta_\alpha$, each $C_{\alpha,\ell}$ is dimensionless in the stated natural units, and the chosen reality conditions make $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{tr}}$ real. This is canonical-dimension counting for the selected linear EFT; HEFT chiral counting and multi-scale SCET counting are different schemes and are not implied. A truncation order is not a numerical error bound, a coefficient prediction, or a derived renormalization-group flow.

If the same application also uses a finite-regulator data record, retain its graph variables, measure, Wilsonian scale $\mu_W$, heavy mass $M$, external-energy bound $E$, and regulator cutoff $\Lambda$ with their supplied meanings. The operator-suppression scale $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}$, regulator cutoff $\Lambda$, $M$, $E$, and $\mu_W$ are distinct parameters unless an additional model input identifies them. A map from finite-graph variables to the continuum finite-jet operator data is also additional input; the finite-regulator definition supplies no such map or continuum limit.

manifest_declaration.title: CLs ratio for source-specified signal exclusions
manifest_declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; current readiness is recorded separately.
manifest_declaration.statement:
Let $(S,\mathcal S)$ be a data space with two supplied probability laws $\mathbb P_b$ and $\mathbb P_{s+b}$ for the background-only and signal-plus-background hypotheses. Fix a statistic $T:S\to\mathbb R$ for which larger values are more incompatible with the signal-plus-background hypothesis and for which every upper-tail set is measurable. For observed datum $x\in S$, set $R_x:=\{y\in S:T(y)\ge T(x)\}$ and define
$$\mathrm{CL}_b(x):=\mathbb P_b(R_x),\qquad \mathrm{CL}_{s+b}(x):=\mathbb P_{s+b}(R_x).$$
When $\mathrm{CL}_b(x)>0$, the modified-frequentist exclusion ratio is
$$\mathrm{CL}_s(x):=\frac{\mathrm{CL}_{s+b}(x)}{\mathrm{CL}_b(x)}.$$
A reported exclusion rule at threshold $\alpha\in(0,1)$ excludes a specified signal-plus-background hypothesis when its supplied analysis has $\mathrm{CL}_s(x)<\alpha$. The likelihood ratio, test statistic, nuisance treatment, and sampling laws are part of the specified analysis. The ratio is not itself a probability or a frequentist coverage level; in the cited method it is a conservative, frequentist-motivated approximation used to present exclusion results. It does not give the probability that a signal model is true or false.

manifest_declaration.title: Heavy chiral U(1)_V threshold model data
manifest_declaration.design_state: Defines the exact selected H=SU(3)×U(1)_V heavy-chiral threshold model, singlet charge, Yukawa mass, regulator, counterterm convention, and source-backed mass-independent threshold input.
manifest_declaration.physical_scope: A selected perturbative U(1)_V-singlet chiral threshold sector inside H=SU(3)×U(1)_V on the trivial bundle over four-dimensional Minkowski space; no dynamical gauge-consistency or global-anomaly claim.
manifest_declaration.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ on the four-dimensional affine Minkowski space $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, as in the selected HEFT spacetime convention. Use the trivial spin structure, spinor bundle $S=M\times\mathbb C^4$, gamma matrices satisfying $\{\gamma^\mu,\gamma^\nu\}=2\eta^{\mu\nu}I$, chirality operator $\gamma_5=i\gamma^0\gamma^1\gamma^2\gamma^3$, and eigensubbundles $S_\pm=\ker(\gamma_5\mp I)$. Take the trivial bundle for the fixed global symmetry group $H=SU(3)\times U(1)_V$, set the $SU(3)$ background connection to zero, and keep only the nondynamical $U(1)_V$ connection $B\in\Omega_c^1(M,\mathbb R)$ with curvature $G=dB$. Here $U(1)_V=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$ and its charge-$q$ representation is $\rho_q(z)=z^q$ on $\mathbb C$. The background $B$ is not integrated over as a quantum gauge redundancy.

Let $\psi_+\in C_c^\infty(M,S_+\otimes\mathbb C_{(\mathbf1,+1)})$ and $\psi_-\in C_c^\infty(M,S_-\otimes\mathbb C_{(\mathbf1,0)})$ be complex Weyl fields in the indicated $SU(3)\times U(1)_V$ representations. Use $D_q=d+iqB$ on charge-$q$ fields and the fixed Lorentz-scalar chiral Dirac pairing $\bar\psi_+\psi_-$. Let $\Phi=v e^{i\theta}$ be a nonvanishing order-parameter field in $(\mathbf1,+1)$ with fixed modulus $v>0$ and smooth real phase $\theta\in C_c^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$. A dimensionless nonzero Yukawa parameter $y$ gives the mass term $-y\Phi\bar\psi_+\psi_-+\mathrm{h.c.}$, where h.c. denotes Hermitian conjugation, and heavy mass $M_H=|y|v>0$. The fermion fields have mass dimension $3/2$, $v$ and $M_H$ have mass dimension one, $B_\mu$ has mass dimension one, $G_{\mu\nu}$ has mass dimension two, and $\theta$ is dimensionless.

For $\alpha\in C_c^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$, use $B\mapsto B+d\alpha$, $\psi_+\mapsto e^{-i\alpha}\psi_+$, $\psi_-\mapsto\psi_-$, and $\Phi\mapsto e^{-i\alpha}\Phi$, hence $\theta\mapsto\theta-\alpha$. These transformations leave the Yukawa term invariant. In the anti-Hermitian product-group convention, the selected singlet has connection $iB$ and covariant derivative $d+iB$; in Bilal's Hermitian convention write $\mathscr A=-B$ and $\epsilon=-\alpha$, so $d-i\mathscr A=d+iB$ and the transformations agree. Let $\Gamma_H[B,\theta]$ denote the formal one-loop effective-action contribution of this fermion pair with the Pauli–Villars subtraction used for the chiral triangle: include a physical loop with $M_0=0$ and three regulator loops with statistics weights $\eta_0=\eta_2=1$ and $\eta_1=\eta_3=-1$, choose a positive scale $M_{\mathrm{PV}}$ and masses $M_1=M_3=M_{\mathrm{PV}}$, $M_2=\sqrt2M_{\mathrm{PV}}$, and take $M_{\mathrm{PV}}\to\infty$ after the subtraction. Define the consistent anomaly as the infinitesimal variation of this effective action, rather than as a covariant-current divergence. Add no non-invariant local counterterm to $\Gamma_H$; gauge-invariant local counterterms may be added. For an undetermined real coefficient $c$, the candidate Wess–Zumino functional is $\Gamma_c[B,\theta]=c\int_M\theta G\wedge G$; the theorem on this page fixes $c$.

As a source-backed threshold input, adopt the following scope-limited consequence of the heavy-fermion field-redefinition argument: removing the phase of a Yukawa-generated heavy chiral mass by a chiral redefinition transfers that phase to the regulated measure, whose consistent anomalous variation is independent of the heavy mass. This supplies the local Wess–Zumino threshold interpretation when $\theta$ is retained; it is not a construction of the full determinant or a bound on all remaining terms. Let $E$ be a positive mass scale bounding absolute external momentum components in these coordinates. The threshold regime is $E/M_H\ll1$, with no Lorentz-invariant norm or expansion-remainder bound asserted. All determinant and anomaly data here are formal perturbative inputs; no exact functional integral or continuum limit is claimed.

manifest_declaration.title: Profile likelihood ratios with nuisance parameters
manifest_declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; current readiness is recorded separately.
manifest_declaration.statement:
Let $(S,\mathcal S)$ be a measurable data space, let $\nu$ be a measure on it, and let $\Psi$ and $H$ be nonempty parameter sets. For each $(\psi,\eta)\in\Psi\times H$, let $p_{\psi,\eta}:S\to[0,+\infty]$ be a specified measurable density with $\int_S p_{\psi,\eta}\,d\nu=1$. A specified pointwise version of each density is part of the model because an observed-data likelihood can depend on the representative chosen within an almost-everywhere equivalence class. The coordinate $\psi$ is the parameter of interest; $\eta$ is a nuisance coordinate, meaning that it is retained in the probability model but is not the parameter whose value is tested or reported. The common dominating measure $\nu$ and the full density family are part of the model.

For observed data $s\in S$, define the likelihood $L_s(\psi,\eta)=p_{\psi,\eta}(s)$. Take both suprema below in the extended real line and suppose the global supremum
$$M_s:=\sup_{(\psi',\eta')\in\Psi\times H}L_s(\psi',\eta')$$
satisfies $0<M_s<+\infty$. For each $\psi\in\Psi$, define the profile likelihood $M_s(\psi)=\sup_{\eta\in H}L_s(\psi,\eta)$ and the profile likelihood ratio
$$\lambda_s(\psi):=\frac{M_s(\psi)}{M_s}\in[0,1].$$
The associated likelihood-ratio statistic is
$$q_s(\psi):=\begin{cases}-2\log\lambda_s(\psi),&\lambda_s(\psi)>0,\\ +\infty,&\lambda_s(\psi)=0,\end{cases}$$
where $\log$ is the real natural logarithm on $(0,\infty)$. These definitions use suprema and do not require a maximizing parameter value to exist. The distribution of $q_s$, a p-value calibration, and the coverage of a confidence set require additional model and sampling assumptions; none follows from this definition.

manifest_declaration.title: Finite renormalization schemes and Wilson coefficient vectors
manifest_declaration.design_state: Defines a fixed-weight complex quotient coefficient interface and supplied truncated RG data; no QFT beta function or omitted-term estimate is asserted.
manifest_declaration.statement:
Work in four spacetime dimensions and natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Fix an
engineering weight $d\in\mathbb Q$ and take as input a finite-dimensional
complex quotient $V=\mathcal Q_d$ of local operators at that fixed weight, with
an ordered basis of representatives $O_1,\ldots,O_N$ and $N=\dim_{\mathbb C}V\ge1$.
The quotient and its declared relations are supplied data; this definition does
not assert that every relation relevant to an EFT, observable, or infinite
operator tower has been included. Each $O_i$ has the same engineering weight
$d$. For a fixed cutoff $\Lambda>0$ of mass dimension one, a coefficient vector
$C=(C_1,\ldots,C_N)\in\mathbb C^N$ determines the formal coefficient
expression in $V$
$$\sum_{i=1}^N\frac{C_i O_i}{\Lambda^{d-4}}.$$
Each $C_i$ is dimensionless, and each summand has mass dimension four. This is
a formal expression in the supplied quotient, not a constructed action. No
Hermiticity or reality condition is imposed; a real-action condition is
additional conjugation data.

A finite scheme record consists of a nonempty set $B$ of input labels, an open
interval $J\subset(0,\infty)$ of renormalization scales, and supplied
coefficient-coordinate maps
$$\mathcal R_\mu:B\longrightarrow\mathbb C^N\qquad(\mu\in J).$$
The maps encode the chosen subtraction and normalization convention and are
not constructed here. For $b\in B$, the scale-dependent Wilson coefficient
vector is $C_{\mathcal R}(\mu;b):=\mathcal R_\mu(b)$. The scale $\mu$ and
cutoff $\Lambda$ are distinct inputs. Choose a reference scale $\mu_0\in J$
and set
$$t:=\log(\mu/\mu_0),\qquad I:=\{\log(\mu/\mu_0):\mu\in J\};$$
then $t$ is dimensionless and $I$ is an open interval containing $0$.

Use the Euclidean norm $\|C\|_2^2=\sum_{i=1}^N|C_i|^2$ on $\mathbb C^N$.
Define the realification $\rho_N:\mathbb C^N\to\mathbb R^{2N}$ by
$$\rho_N(C_1,\ldots,C_N)=(\operatorname{Re}C_1,\operatorname{Im}C_1,\ldots,\operatorname{Re}C_N,\operatorname{Im}C_N).$$
With the Euclidean norm on $\mathbb R^{2N}$, $\rho_N$ is a real-linear
isometry. A supplied finite-dimensional truncated RG datum for this scheme
is an open set $\Omega\subset I\times\mathbb R^{2N}$ and a supplied
continuous map $\beta:\Omega\to\mathbb R^{2N}$. A truncated RG trajectory is
a continuously differentiable curve $C:I'\to\mathbb C^N$, on an interval
$I'\subset I$ for which $(t,\rho_N(C(t)))\in\Omega$, satisfying
$$\frac{d}{dt}\rho_N(C(t))=\beta(t,\rho_N(C(t))).$$
The components of $\beta$ are the beta functions under this logarithmic-scale
convention. If the supplied flow is complex-linear, with a supplied matrix
function $\Gamma:I'\to\mathbb C^{N\times N}$, its equation can be written
$C'=\Gamma(t)C$, where the real-coordinate vector field is
$\beta(t,\rho_N(C))=\rho_N(\Gamma(t)C)$. In this column-vector convention,
$\Gamma$ is called the anomalous-dimension matrix. A scheme record does not
assert that its coefficient-coordinate maps solve a supplied RG equation; that
relation, the entries of $\beta$, and any matching map are separate inputs.
This definition calculates no QFT beta function and supplies no bound on
omitted perturbative or higher-dimension terms.

manifest_declaration.title: Finite-order EFT threshold matching map
manifest_declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; planned item contract; readiness recorded separately.
manifest_declaration.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ and Minkowski signature $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-,+,+,+)$. Fix a reference renormalization scale $\mu_0>0$ and a common open interval $J\subset(0,\infty)$ of renormalization scales $\mu$, with $\mu_0\in J$. Write $t=\log(\mu/\mu_0)$, so $t$ is dimensionless. A threshold datum consists of a high-energy description, denoted $+$, and a lower-energy effective description, denoted $-$. The descriptions have a common declared light-field sector and differ by the degrees of freedom retained across a specified threshold of mass $M>0$. The external-energy domain and the range of validity of the local expansion are supplied separately; in a heavy-particle expansion they ordinarily require external energy $E_{\mathrm{ext}}<M$. The Wilsonian matching scale $\mu_W$, the renormalization scale $\mu$, the threshold mass $M$, the external-energy bound $E_{\mathrm{ext}}$, and the regulator cutoff $\Lambda_{\mathrm{reg}}$ (denoted $\Lambda$ in the finite-regulator model data) have mass dimension one and are distinct data; no equality between $\mu_W$ and $\mu$ is part of this definition.

For each sign $\sigma\in\{+,-\}$, supply a finite coefficient-coordinate space $\mathbb C^{N_\sigma}$ with $N_\sigma\ge1$, a declared ordered operator basis and power-counting truncation, and a renormalization-scheme coordinate map. Any identification of the Wilsonian coefficient data at $\mu_W$ with these scheme coordinates is supplied input; this definition does not identify $\mu_W$ with $\mu$. The vector $C_\sigma(t)\in\mathbb C^{N_\sigma}$ is the column of dimensionless Wilson coefficients in that basis. The corresponding finite-order operator expression uses the supplied convention $C_{\sigma,i}O_{\sigma,i}/\Lambda_{\mathrm{op},\sigma}^{d_i-4}$, with each $O_{\sigma,i}$ of engineering dimension $d_i$ and $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op},\sigma}>0$ the coefficient-suppression scale for that theory, denoted $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}$ in its physical operator contract and $\Lambda$ in the generic scheme convention. It is distinct from $\Lambda_{\mathrm{reg}}$, $M$, $E_{\mathrm{ext}}$, $\mu_W$, and $\mu$ unless additional model data identify some of them. Write $\rho_{N_\sigma}$ for the realification that lists the real and imaginary parts of each coefficient. A supplied RG vector field is a continuous map $\beta_\sigma:\Omega_\sigma\to\mathbb R^{2N_\sigma}$ on a supplied open domain $\Omega_\sigma\subset J\times\mathbb R^{2N_\sigma}$; an RG trajectory satisfies
$$\frac{d}{dt}\rho_{N_\sigma}(C_\sigma(t))=\beta_\sigma(t,\rho_{N_\sigma}(C_\sigma(t))).$$
For each sign, the physical operator datum is an instance of the selected physical EFT operator contract. It specifies finitely many field species and jet generators, finite-dimensional graded field spaces, smooth field domains and regularity, reality data, and rational engineering weights. Even fields are smooth maps; odd components take values in a fixed Grassmann algebra with smooth coefficient functions.

The Lorentz action is that of the proper orthochronous group
$SO^+(1,3)=\{L\in GL_4(\mathbb R):L^T\eta L=\eta,\ \det L=1,\ L^0{}_0\ge1\}$,
and each Lagrangian density is a Lorentz scalar. The datum gives the full gauge
and flavor actions on fields, indices, and spurions. A spurion is a fixed
non-dynamical parameter used to record a declared symmetry-breaking insertion;
absent flavor symmetry is recorded as trivial, and broken symmetry requires
its spurions and weights.

The datum fixes finite derivative, field-degree, dimension, and loop cutoffs,
the relation subspace and representatives, and a complex reductive affine
algebraic group with maps relating its representations to the physical gauge
and flavor groups. Here reductive means there is no nontrivial closed normal
unipotent subgroup; unipotent means every nonzero finite-dimensional rational
module has a nonzero fixed vector. On each retained jet space the data either
verify that the algebraic invariant subspace equals the intended physical
invariant space or label the quotient as a formal algebraic selection only.

Each relation generator is recorded as a polynomial or Fierz identity, a total
divergence with compact-support or stated boundary conditions, or a
leading-equation/field-redefinition relation tied to a base action and retained
order. The latter records its variational derivative, multiplier, inverse
through the retained order, and induced higher-order terms. This quotient alone
does not establish action, off-shell Green-function, quantum-measure, or
scattering equivalence.

If a non-Abelian gauge sector is selected, its actual compact real global group
(compact meaning every open cover has a finite subcover), smooth right
principal bundle (with smooth free and transitive right action and equivariant
local trivializations), admitted bundle sectors, and unitary representations
(actions preserving specified positive-definite Hermitian forms) are part of
the data. A selected smooth principal connection uses the right-action
convention $Z_P(p):=\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_0p\exp_G(tZ)$,
$\omega_p(Z_P(p))=Z$, and $R_g(p)=pg$,
$R_g^*\omega=\operatorname{Ad}_{g^{-1}}\omega$, where
$\operatorname{Ad}_g=d(C_g)_e$ and $C_g(h)=ghg^{-1}$. Locally, for
$A=s^*\omega$ and a representation $\rho$ with $\rho_*:=d\rho_e$, its
curvature and associated covariant derivative are
$F_A=dA+\tfrac12[A\wedge A]$ and
$D_\mu=\partial_\mu+\rho_*(A_\mu)$, using the supplied graded Lie-bracket
convention. Each finite basis represents only this supplied fixed-order
quotient; no completeness claim about all physical relations or an infinite
operator tower is made. These field and counting inputs are not inferred from
coefficient coordinates.
For $x\in\mathbb R^{2N_\sigma}$, write $\Phi_\sigma(t,s)x\in\mathbb R^{2N_\sigma}$ for the value at $t$ of the unique realified coefficient solution with value $x$ at $s$, whenever a unique such solution exists on the interval between $s$ and $t$.

A declared matching calculation supplies a finite list of renormalized amplitudes or Green-function values $A_{\sigma,j}(t,c;\lambda_{\mathrm{IR}})$, where $j$ indexes the selected external states and kinematics, $c$ is a coefficient vector, and $\lambda_{\mathrm{IR}}$ denotes the common infrared regulator used in both descriptions. Let $U_\sigma\subset\mathbb C^{N_\sigma}$ be open coefficient domains for $\sigma\in\{+,-\}$. The supplied matching family is a jointly continuously differentiable real map $\widehat{\mathcal M}:\mathcal V\to\rho_{N_-}(U_-)$ on an open domain $\mathcal V\subset J\times\rho_{N_+}(U_+)$. Its admissible domain is the open subset $\mathcal U=\{(t,x)\in\mathcal V:(t,x)\in\Omega_+,\ (t,\widehat{\mathcal M}(t,x))\in\Omega_-\}$. It defines $M_t(c):=\rho_{N_-}^{-1}(\widehat{\mathcal M}(t,\rho_{N_+}(c)))$ for each admitted $(t,c)$, and $\widehat M_t(x):=\widehat{\mathcal M}(t,x)$ on the corresponding slice. Thus the scale derivative and coefficient derivative in the compatibility condition below both exist and are continuous. It is a matching map through the declared loop order, operator dimension, and mass-expansion order when, for every selected $j$ and every admitted pair $(t,c)$ with $c\in U_+$, the prescribed truncations of $A_{+,j}(t,c;\lambda_{\mathrm{IR}})$ and $A_{-,j}(t,M_t(c);\lambda_{\mathrm{IR}})$ agree. The truncation projection and its retained orders are part of the datum. This equality records only the selected amplitudes and orders; it neither estimates discarded terms nor asserts that a matching calculation exists for every model.

A matching map is RG-compatible on these domains when, in realified coefficient coordinates,
$$\partial_t\widehat M_t(x)+D_x\widehat M_t(x)\,\beta_+(t,x)=\beta_-\!\left(t,\widehat M_t(x)\right)$$
for every admitted $(t,x)$. Here $D_x$ is the ordinary real derivative with respect to the coefficient coordinates. RG-compatibility is an additional condition to be checked from the supplied beta functions and matching calculation; it does not follow merely from defining $M_t$ by amplitude equality.

For several thresholds, let $t_1>\cdots>t_k$ be their logarithmic scales, let $\Phi_j$ be the realified evolution in the theory active between thresholds $t_j$ and $t_{j+1}$, and let $\widehat M_j(t_j)$ map realified coefficient data from the theory above threshold $j$ to the theory below it. The ordered high-to-low transport is
$$\Phi_k(t_f,t_k)\circ\widehat M_k(t_k)\circ\Phi_{k-1}(t_k,t_{k-1})\circ\cdots\circ\widehat M_1(t_1)\circ\Phi_0(t_1,t_i),$$
whenever all displayed flows and matching maps are defined. This definition specifies supplied finite-order data and their conventions; it computes no beta-function entry or matching coefficient and asserts no continuum limit.

manifest_declaration.title: Supersymmetric Wilsonian EFT action and threshold data
manifest_declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; planned item contract; readiness recorded separately.
manifest_declaration.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$, flat spacetime $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$, coordinates $x^0=ct$, and metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. A local rigid four-dimensional $\mathcal N=1$ supersymmetric Wilsonian action datum uses finitely many smooth classical chiral superfields $\Phi_i$ and, when a gauge sector is selected, a stated compact global gauge group, unitary field representations, and its specified vector-superfield data. A chiral field obeys $\bar D_{\dot\alpha}\Phi_i=0$; the scalar and Weyl-spinor components have the dimensions fixed by $[\Phi_i]=1$, while $[W_\alpha]=3/2$ for the chiral gauge-field-strength superfield. The action has the superspace form

$$\mathcal L_\lambda=[\sum_i\Phi_i^\dagger e^{-V_i}\Phi_i+G_\lambda]_D+2\operatorname{Re}[\frac{\tau_\lambda}{8\pi i}\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm h}(W^\alpha W_\alpha)+F_\lambda(\Phi,W)]_F,$$

where the physical action brackets are $[U]_D=-I_D(U)/4$, $[Y]_F=I_F(Y)/2$ from [[def-qftx-physical-superspace-normalization]], with physical chiral components $\psi_{\mathrm{raw}}=\sqrt2\psi$, $F_{\mathrm{raw}}=2F$, and $G_\lambda$ is real and gauge invariant, $F_\lambda$ is holomorphic, gauge invariant, and has no superspace or spacetime derivatives, $[\tau_\lambda]=0$, and the chiral and real terms are respectively called the Wilsonian F-term and D-term. The cutoff prescription is formal and coefficientwise at a nonzero Wilsonian mode scale $0<\lambda<\Lambda_0$; it supplies a local derivative expansion and claims neither convergence nor a continuum functional measure. A one-particle-irreducible vertex is a vertex contribution that cannot be disconnected by cutting one internal propagator; it is separate data from the Wilsonian action.

A finite supersymmetric EFT operator datum selects finitely many field species, coefficient spaces and Grassmann parities, their gauge and flavor actions, and a maximum spacetime-jet order $r$. A field jet is a component of a field or one of its spacetime derivatives $\partial_I\Phi_i$ for a multi-index $I$ with $|I|\le r$. It also selects a coefficient field, spurions, maximum engineering weight $D_{\max}$, field-degree cutoff $q$, loop cutoff $L_{\max}$, and a finite ordered basis $\mathcal O_\alpha$ for the declared quotient $\mathcal Q_D=V_D/R_D$ of invariant local polynomials by the explicitly supplied relation subspace. Each $\mathcal O_\alpha$ is a Lorentz-scalar representative built from finitely many such jets and has the declared gauge/flavor transformation law and engineering weight $\Delta_\alpha$. Each retained coefficient $C_{\alpha,\ell}$ is dimensionless in the convention

$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{tr}}=\sum_{\Delta_\alpha\le D_{\max}}\sum_{\ell=0}^{L_{\max}}\zeta^\ell C_{\alpha,\ell}(\mu_W)\frac{\mathcal O_\alpha}{\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}^{\Delta_\alpha-4}},$$

where $\zeta$ is formal loop bookkeeping, $\Delta_\alpha$ is the engineering weight of $\mathcal O_\alpha$, and $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}>0$ is its coefficient-suppression scale. The declared relations may include polynomial or Fierz identities, superspace integration by parts under stated compact-support or boundary conditions, gauge identities, and leading-superfield-equation relations. Every equation-of-motion or field-redefinition relation records its base action, parity-preserving local identity-leading map, inverse through the retained order, and all induced terms. This quotient records only the supplied relations and does not assert that it is a complete physical basis.

An optional on-shell amplitude-equivalence record for such a relation includes a local, parity-preserving formal field map with identity leading term and inverse through the retained order, an invariant action for the declared complex reductive symmetry, the exact finite-regulator change-of-variables density and its Jacobian, the correspondingly transformed source, and a common regulator limit with stable positive-mass simple poles, nonzero residues, and the stated LSZ pole factorization. Under full Axiom of Choice, the fixed-order equivalence theorem applies to that record and its exact hypotheses. The quotient alone does not identify off-shell Green functions or prove that a regulator, its Jacobian, or an LSZ limit exists.

For one declared threshold, the high-energy and low-energy descriptions share their specified light fields and differ by a nonempty declared heavy-multiplet sector of threshold mass $M>0$. A finite matching record supplies the high- and low-energy coefficient spaces and bases, selected renormalized amplitudes or Green functions, their common infrared regulator, external states and kinematics, matching map, and retained loop, operator, and mass-expansion orders. The Wilsonian scale $\mu_W$, renormalization scale $\mu$, heavy threshold mass $M$, external-energy bound $E_{\mathrm{ext}}$, regulator cutoff $\Lambda_{\mathrm{reg}}$, and operator-suppression scale $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}$ all have mass dimension one and are distinct unless additional model data identify them. Matching equality concerns only the selected amplitudes and stated truncation; it supplies no discarded-term error bound and is not an equality of arbitrary one-particle-irreducible functionals.

manifest_declaration.title: Equivariant elliptic-complex index and character
manifest_declaration.statement:
Let $T$ be a compact torus and $M$ a compact smooth manifold without boundary. A smooth left $T$-action is a jointly smooth map $a:T\times M\to M$ with $a(e,x)=x$ and $a(st,x)=a(s,a(t,x))$. Let $E^0,\ldots,E^N$ be finite-rank complex vector bundles on $M$. For each $j<N$, let $d_j:C^\infty(M,E^j)\to C^\infty(M,E^{j+1})$ be a linear differential operator of finite order, and put $d_{-1}=d_N=0$. The sequence is a complex when $d_{j+1}d_j=0$ for every $j$. It is **elliptic** when, for every $x\in M$ and every nonzero real cotangent vector $\xi\in T_x^*M$, the sequence of principal-symbol maps

$$0\longrightarrow E_x^0\xrightarrow{\sigma(d_0)(x,\xi)}E_x^1\xrightarrow{\sigma(d_1)(x,\xi)}\cdots\xrightarrow{\sigma(d_{N-1})(x,\xi)}E_x^N\longrightarrow0$$

is exact. Suppose each bundle has a smooth $T$-linearization $\rho_t^j:E_x^j\to E_{t\cdot x}^j$, satisfying the group-action law, and the induced section maps

$$ (U_t^j s)(x):=\rho_t^j\bigl(s(t^{-1}\cdot x)\bigr) $$

commute with $d_j$. Require the cohomology spaces $H^j(E^\bullet):=\ker d_j/\operatorname{im}d_{j-1}$ to be finite-dimensional. The representation ring $R(T)$ is the Grothendieck ring of finite-dimensional continuous complex representations of $T$. Define

$$\operatorname{Ind}_T(E^\bullet):=\sum_{j=0}^N(-1)^j[H^j(E^\bullet)]\in R(T),\qquad \chi_{E^\bullet}(t):=\sum_{j=0}^N(-1)^j\operatorname{tr}\!\left(U_t^j\bigm|_{H^j(E^\bullet)}\right).$$

For a two-term complex $0\to C^\infty(M,E^+)\xrightarrow{D^+}C^\infty(M,E^-)\to0$, this gives $[\ker D^+]-[\operatorname{coker}D^+]$. This definition concerns elliptic complexes, not transversally elliptic operators.

manifest_declaration.title: Finite-Dimensional Q-Exact Localization Data
manifest_declaration.statement:
Let $M$ be an oriented smooth manifold of finite dimension $n$, with a chosen integration cycle and a smooth positive volume form $\mu$. Its parity-reversed tangent bundle $\Pi TM$ has even base coordinates $x^1,\ldots,x^n$ and odd fiber coordinates $\theta^1,\ldots,\theta^n$, which transform as the coordinate one-forms $dx^i$. Smooth functions on $\Pi TM$ are identified with inhomogeneous complex differential forms $\mathcal A=\Omega^\bullet(M;\mathbb C)$; the parity of a form is its degree modulo two. The Berezin convention is $\int d\theta^n\cdots d\theta^1\,\theta^1\cdots\theta^n=1$. For $F\in\mathcal A$, write $F_{[n]}=f_F\mu$ for its degree-$n$ component and define the graded integral by $I_\Gamma(F):=\int_M f_F\,d\mu=\int_M F_{[n]}$, equivalently by Berezin integration over the odd fibers followed by integration over the body $M$ with the chosen orientation.

A supercharge $Q$ is a smooth odd derivation of $\mathcal A$, so for homogeneous forms $\alpha,\beta$ it satisfies $Q(\alpha\wedge\beta)=Q\alpha\wedge\beta+(-1)^{|\alpha|}\alpha\wedge Q\beta$. Its square $Q^2:=Q\circ Q$ is an even derivation. The measure and cycle are $Q$-invariant on an admissible class of integrands when $I_\Gamma(QF)=0$ for every $F$ in that class. The associated Berezinian density on $\Pi TM$ has local expression $dx^1\cdots dx^n\,d\theta^n\cdots d\theta^1$ in oriented coordinates. In that coordinate description, zero divergence means $\mathcal L_Q\boldsymbol\mu_\Pi=(\operatorname{div}_{\boldsymbol\mu_\Pi}Q)\boldsymbol\mu_\Pi=0$, together with vanishing boundary flux. Compact support in the interior or explicit decay may impose the boundary condition on a noncompact or bounded cycle.

An admissible finite-dimensional $Q$-exact deformation consists of even smooth forms $S,O\in\mathcal A$, an odd smooth form $V\in\mathcal A$, and an open interval $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ such that $QS=QO=0$. The even form $QV$ is the $Q$-exact deformation, $S_t:=S+tQV$, and $E_t:=e^{-S_t}$, with the exponential defined by the usual pointwise exponential of its degree-zero part and the finite exterior-degree expansion of its positive-degree part. Require $(Q^2V)E_t=0$ for every $t\in J$; the stronger condition $Q^2V=0$ is sufficient. Require $O E_t$ and $O V E_t$ to be admissible integrands, with no boundary flux in $I_\Gamma(Q(O V E_t))$.

Write $(O E_t)_{[n]}=f_t\mu$. The deformation data are analytically admissible when $f_t$ is integrable for every $t\in J$, $t\mapsto f_t(x)$ is differentiable for almost every $x$, $\partial_t f_t$ is measurable, and for every compact $K\subset J$ there is a single nonnegative $g_K\in L^1(M,\mu)$ such that $|f_t(x)|\le g_K(x)$ and $|\partial_t f_t(x)|\le g_K(x)$ for every $t\in K$ outside one $\mu$-null set. The underlying manifold is finite-dimensional; its smooth-function algebra need not be finite-dimensional as a vector space.

manifest_declaration.title: ADHM linear data, stability, costability and FI levels
manifest_declaration.statement:
Fix integers $N\ge1$ and $k\ge0$ and standard Hermitian spaces $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$. A framed ADHM linear datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$ and $J:V\to W$. Define the complex and real polynomial expressions

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable if the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, with $m\ge0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$ and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable if there is no nonzero subspace of $V$ invariant under both $B_i$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular if it is stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$. Its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$.

Write $X^s=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable}\}$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}=\{x\in X^s:x\text{ costable}\}$ and, for real $\zeta\ge0$, $X_\zeta^U=\{x\in X^s:\mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=\zeta I_V\}$. Denote the corresponding orbit sets by $X^s/GL(V)$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}/GL(V)$ and $X_\zeta^U/U(V)$, with quotient topologies when discussing their analytic spaces. A word frame consists of $k$ columns obtained by fixed words in $B_1,B_2$ applied to fixed standard basis vectors of $W$.

For $T_{\mathbb C}=(\mathbb C^*)^2\times(\mathbb C^*)^N$, write $t_1,t_2,e_1,\ldots,e_N$ for the coordinate characters and put $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. Its action is $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot x=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$. The compact torus is its subgroup on which all characters have modulus one. The framing representation thus has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$ and its dual has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$.

These are finite-dimensional matrix definitions. They do not assert a real/complex quotient correspondence, a sheaf or ASD identification, or a noncompact pushforward. In particular, positive-FI stability and zero-FI regularity are distinct conditions; neither an endpoint identification nor an ordinary ASD interpretation follows from this definition.

manifest_declaration.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Use natural units $\hbar=c=1$ on Minkowski spacetime $\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, orientation $dt\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, and spatial orientation $\epsilon_{123}=1$. Fix the global gauge group $SU(2)$, not $SO(3)$, and the trivial right principal $SU(2)$-bundle over each spatial slice. Let

$$T_a=-\frac{i}{2}\sigma_a\quad(a=1,2,3),\qquad \kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY),$$

where $\sigma_a$ are the Pauli matrices and $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ has basis $T_1,T_2,T_3$. Thus $[T_a,T_b]=\epsilon_{abc}T_c$ and $\kappa(T_a,T_b)=\delta_{ab}$. The positive coupling $g$ is dimensionless. The scalar field is one real adjoint Higgs field: a smooth $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued map $\Phi$ on $\mathbb R^3$, viewed as the real form in the complexified adjoint representation. A gauge connection is a smooth $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued one-form $A=A_i dx^i$. In a local section change $s_j=s_i h_{ij}$, use the right-action convention $A_j=\operatorname{Ad}_{h_{ij}^{-1}}A_i+h_{ij}^{-1}dh_{ij}$ and $\Phi_j=\operatorname{Ad}_{h_{ij}^{-1}}\Phi_i$. Define

$$F_{ij}=\partial_iA_j-\partial_jA_i+[A_i,A_j],\qquad D_i\Phi=\partial_i\Phi+[A_i,\Phi],\qquad B_i=\frac12\epsilon_{ijk}F_{jk}.$$

The static Prasad–Sommerfield sector has $\partial_tA_i=\partial_t\Phi=0$, $A_0=0$, no other dynamical fields, and identically zero Higgs potential. Its adopted energy functional is

$$E[A,\Phi]=\frac{1}{2g^2}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\sum_{i=1}^3\bigl(\kappa(B_i,B_i)+\kappa(D_i\Phi,D_i\Phi)\bigr)\,d^3x.$$

The field dimensions are $[A_i]=[\Phi]=\mathrm{length}^{-1}$ and $[F_{ij}]=[B_i]=[D_i\Phi]=\mathrm{length}^{-2}$, so $E$ has dimension $\mathrm{length}^{-1}$. A configuration is finite-energy when this integral is finite.

The boundary data fix a number $v>0$ of dimension $\mathrm{length}^{-1}$ and require $|\Phi|_\kappa\to v$ and $n_\infty(\omega):=\lim_{R\to\infty}\Phi(R\omega)/v$ to exist smoothly on the unit sphere $S^2$ of spatial directions. Here $|X|_\kappa^2:=\kappa(X,X)$. The limiting tangential covariant derivative of $n_\infty$ vanishes, and the limiting magnetic field lies in the pointwise stabilizer Lie algebra $\{X\in\mathfrak{su}(2):[X,n_\infty(\omega)]=0\}$. The stabilizer subgroup of $T_3$ is $U(1)=\{\exp(\theta T_3):\theta\in\mathbb R/(4\pi\mathbb Z)\}$. On closed northern and southern hemispheres choose smooth local lifts $u_N,u_S$ with $\operatorname{Ad}_{u_\alpha}T_3=n_\infty$; their equatorial transition is $u_S=u_N h$ with $h(\varphi)=\exp(\theta(\varphi)T_3)$, where $\varphi\in[0,2\pi]$ parametrizes the equator and $\theta:[0,2\pi]\to\mathbb R$ is a smooth lift. The local adapted frames, connection forms, and curvature forms extend smoothly, respectively $C^1$, to open neighborhoods of the closed hemispheres. The surface limit below exists. The admissible external Wilson probes include the fundamental doublet, on which $T_3$ has weights $\pm\tfrac12$; this specifies the electric probe lattice without adding a propagating fundamental matter field. Define the classical magnetic surface charge and its energy normalization by

$$m:=\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_{S_R^2}\kappa(\Phi,B_i)\,\hat x_i\,dS,\qquad T:=g^{-2}m,$$

where $\hat x=x/|x|$ is the outward unit normal and $dS$ is Euclidean area. The transition increment $\theta(2\pi)-\theta(0)$ is not assumed to be quantized in this definition. These are adopted classical model data; they assert no empirical law, quantum continuum construction, supersymmetry representation, or quantum BPS state.

manifest_declaration.title: Coherent module sheaves on complex manifolds
manifest_declaration.statement:
Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space, so $X$ is a topological space and $\mathcal O_X$ is a sheaf of commutative rings. An $\mathcal O_X$-module sheaf $\mathcal F$ is **locally of finite type** if for every $x\in X$ there are an open neighborhood $U$ of $x$, a finite integer $r\ge0$, and sections $s_1,\ldots,s_r\in\mathcal F(U)$ such that their germs generate $\mathcal F_y$ as an $\mathcal O_{X,y}$-module for every $y\in U$.

For an open $V\subseteq X$, a finite integer $p\ge0$, and an $\mathcal O_X$-module morphism $\phi:\mathcal O_V^{\oplus p}\to\mathcal F|_V$, its **relation sheaf** is the kernel sheaf $\ker\phi$. The module sheaf $\mathcal F$ is **coherent** if it is locally of finite type and, for every such $V$, $p$, and $\phi$, the relation sheaf $\ker\phi$ is locally of finite type. Here $\mathcal O_V^{\oplus0}$ is the zero module sheaf.

In particular, for a finite tuple $f_1,\ldots,f_p\in\mathcal O_X(U)$, its holomorphic relation sheaf is the kernel of the morphism $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus p}\to\mathcal O_U$ that sends $(a_1,\ldots,a_p)$ to $\sum_{j=1}^p a_jf_j$. The structure sheaf is coherent when it is coherent as a module over itself. If $M$ is a complex manifold, an **analytic coherent module on $M$** means a coherent module sheaf over its sheaf $\mathcal O_M$ of holomorphic functions.

manifest_declaration.title: Positive incidence geometry for the coupled Penrose transform
manifest_declaration.design_state: Authored in batch 68; no design section governs this pair.
manifest_declaration.statement:
Let $S^4={X\in\mathbb R^5:|X|=1}$ have its unit round metric and the orientation which, on the stereographic chart $S^4\setminus\{\infty\}\cong\mathbb R^4$, is $dx_0\wedge dx_1\wedge dx_2\wedge dx_3$. Put $z_1=x_0+ix_1$, $z_2=x_2+ix_3$, and $r^2=|z_1|^2+|z_2|^2$; in these coordinates the metric is $g=4(1+r^2)^{-2}\sum_{\mu=0}^3dx_\mu^2$. Identify $\mathbb H^2$ with $\mathbb C^4$ using a right quaternionic structure $j$ with $j^2=-1$, put $Z=\mathbb CP^3=\mathbb P_{\mathbb C}(\mathbb H^2)$, and define $\pi:Z\to\mathbb HP^1=S^4$ by $\pi(\ell)=\ell+j\ell$ for a complex line $\ell\subset\mathbb H^2$. Its fibres are projective lines $L_x\cong\mathbb CP^1$. In homogeneous coordinates $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]$, the fibre over finite $z=(z_1,z_2)$ is the line

$$\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2,\qquad \mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2,$$

and the fibre over infinity is $L_\infty=\{\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0\}$. Give $Z$ the Fubini–Study metric induced by the standard Hermitian metric on $\mathbb C^4$ and give $\mathcal O_Z(-2)$ its induced Hermitian metric. On the incidence chart $\lambda_1\ne0$, set $t=\lambda_2/\lambda_1$, $\mu_1/\lambda_1=z_1-\bar z_2t$, and $\mu_2/\lambda_1=z_2+\bar z_1t$. The horizontal complex directions of type $(0,1)$ are spanned by

$$H_1=\partial_{\bar z_1}-t\partial_{z_2},\qquad H_2=\partial_{\bar z_2}+t\partial_{z_1};$$

They annihilate the displayed holomorphic coordinates. Together with $\partial_{\bar t}$ they form a direct local frame of $T^{0,1}Z$. Here $H_i$ are the constant-$t$ chart lifts; their projected complex alpha-plane is intrinsic, but this chart splitting is not asserted to be the global metric splitting. Globally let $V^{0,1}=\ker(d\pi)\cap T^{0,1}Z$, and let $H^{0,1}$ be its Fubini–Study orthogonal complement. Its lifts project to the same alpha-planes and may differ from the displayed $H_i$ by vertical components. All global horizontal/vertical form decompositions use this orthogonal splitting; local computations may use the displayed constant-$t$ splitting after retaining the resulting frame and normalization factors. The second projective chart supplies the same alpha-plane at $t=\infty$. The line bundle $\mathcal O_Z(-1)$ is the tautological holomorphic line bundle and $\mathcal O_Z(-2)=\mathcal O_Z(-1)^{\otimes2}$.

manifest_declaration.title: Critical Abelian Higgs fields, winding and divisor data
manifest_declaration.statement:
Let $e>0$ and $\xi>0$ be real parameters, set $\kappa=2e^2\xi$, identify the oriented Euclidean plane $\mathbb R^2$ with $\mathbb C$ using coordinates $(x_1,x_2)$, and use the Hodge star convention $*dx_1=dx_2$, $*dx_2=-dx_1$. A field pair is a smooth real one-form $A=A_1dx_1+A_2dx_2$ on the trivial complex line over $\mathbb R^2$ and a smooth function $q:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb C$. Its unit-charge covariant derivative is $D_Aq=dq-iAq$, its curvature is $F_A=dA=B\,dx_1\wedge dx_2$ with $B=\partial_1A_2-\partial_2A_1$, and its transverse energy is
$$E(A,q)=\int_{\mathbb R^2}\left(\frac{B^2}{2e^2}+|D_{A,1}q|^2+|D_{A,2}q|^2+\frac{e^2}{2}(|q|^2-\xi)^2\right)dx_1dx_2.$$
The pair has finite energy when this nonnegative Lebesgue integral is finite. An admissible boundary sector consists of an integer $n$, a radius $R_0$, and smooth functions $\rho>0$ and real $2\pi$-periodic $\phi$ on $r>R_0$ such that $q(r,\theta)=\rho(r,\theta)e^{i(n\theta+\phi(r,\theta))}$ and $\rho\to\sqrt\xi$, $\phi\to0$ uniformly as $r\to\infty$; $n$ is its winding. A gauge transformation is $(q,A)\mapsto(e^{i\chi}q,A+d\chi)$ for a smooth real-valued function $\chi$ on $\mathbb R^2$.

For $n\ge0$, the positive critical first-order equations are $(D_{A,1}+iD_{A,2})q=0$ and $B=e^2(\xi-|q|^2)$; for $n\le0$ the negative equations are $(D_{A,1}-iD_{A,2})q=0$ and $B=-e^2(\xi-|q|^2)$. The adjective critical refers to the displayed energy normalization and these square-saturating equations. For a positive-winding solution, its divisor is an effective finite divisor $D=\sum_{j=1}^Jm_j[z_j]$, where the $z_j\in\mathbb C$ are distinct, the multiplicities $m_j$ are positive integers, $q$ vanishes exactly at the $z_j$, and near each $z_j$ it has the local form $q(z)=(z-z_j)^{m_j}g_j(z)$ with $g_j$ smooth and nonzero there. The degree is $N=\sum_jm_j$; the empty divisor has degree zero. Negative winding uses the conjugate field and reversed orientation, with $N=|n|$.

On the complement of the divisor, define $h=\log(|q|^2/\xi)$. The associated scalar Taubes datum is a real function smooth away from the divisor such that $h-2m_j\log|z-z_j|$ extends smoothly across every $z_j$, $h\to0$ at infinity, and, as a distribution,
$$\Delta h+\kappa(1-e^h)=4\pi\sum_{j=1}^Jm_j\delta_{z_j},\qquad \langle\delta_z,\psi\rangle=\psi(z)\quad(\psi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2)).$$
When the limit exists, the magnetic flux is $\Phi(A)=\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_{|x|<R}B(x)\,dx_1dx_2$. These are mathematical configuration and normalization conventions; they make no assertion that a physical model describes nature.

manifest_declaration.title: Fréchet spaces used in analytic coherent cohomology
manifest_declaration.statement:
A **Fréchet space** over $\mathbb C$ is a complex vector space $E$ with a Hausdorff locally convex vector-space topology generated by a separating countable family of seminorms $(p_n)_{n\ge1}$ and complete for its seminorm uniformity. Explicitly, use the translation-invariant compatible metric
$$d(x,y)=\sum_{n\ge1}2^{-n}\min\{1,p_n(x-y)\},$$
and require that this metric is complete. A seminorm is a function $p:E\to[0,\infty)$ satisfying $p(x+y)\le p(x)+p(y)$ and $p(cx)=|c|p(x)$ for $x,y\in E$ and $c\in\mathbb C$; separating means that for $x\ne0$ some $p_n(x)>0$. Locally convex means that every point has a neighborhood basis of convex sets. One may replace the defining family by the increasing family of its finite maxima.

Completeness here always refers to this vector-space uniformity. A sequence is Cauchy for the displayed metric exactly when it is Cauchy for every defining seminorm: each individual metric summand controls that seminorm at sufficiently small distances, and conversely the geometric tail of the metric series plus finitely many seminorm estimates controls the metric. Thus a seminorm-Cauchy series used in the accompanying proofs converges in $E$. The zero vector space is included, with its unique metric. This is the usual complete metrizable locally convex Fréchet convention.

manifest_declaration.title: Presentation and Čech quotient topologies for coherent analytic sections
manifest_declaration.statement:
Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional complex manifold, let $\mathcal O_M$ be its sheaf of holomorphic functions, and let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_M$-module sheaf. On an open set $V$ contained in a coordinate chart and in a neighborhood with a finite presentation $\mathcal O_V^{p_1}\to\mathcal O_V^{p_0}\xrightarrow{\pi}\mathcal F|_V\to0$, where $p_0,p_1$ are finite nonnegative ranks, require that the section map $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V^{p_0})\to\Gamma(V,\mathcal F)$ is surjective. Give $\mathcal O(V)^{p_0}$ the compact-convergence topology generated by the seminorms $f\mapsto\sup_{z\in K}\lVert f(z)\rVert$ for compact $K\subset V$, and give $\Gamma(V,\mathcal F)$ the quotient topology induced by that surjection. On any open subset covered by countably many such sets, use the topology of the closed subspace of the product of their local section spaces consisting of compatible families. For a finite ordered open cover $\mathcal U=(U_i)$ whose nonempty finite intersections have these section topologies, give each Čech cochain space

$$C^q(\mathcal U,\mathcal F):=\prod_{i_0<\cdots<i_q}\Gamma(U_{i_0}\cap\cdots\cap U_{i_q},\mathcal F),\qquad (\delta c)_{i_0\cdots i_{q+1}}=\sum_{\nu=0}^{q+1}(-1)^\nu c_{i_0\cdots\widehat{i_\nu}\cdots i_{q+1}}\big|_{U_{i_0}\cap\cdots\cap U_{i_{q+1}}}.$$

the finite-product topology, give its cocycle space the subspace topology, and give the quotient of cocycles by coboundaries the Čech quotient topology. The accompanying Fréchet-quotient lemma proves local chart and presentation independence; the compact projective-space finiteness theorem proves independence of its admissible finite acyclic cover topology.

manifest_declaration.title: Localized torus-equivariant Borel–Moore classes
manifest_declaration.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $r\geq 0$, let $T=(\mathbb C^\times)^r$ act algebraically on a separated finite-type complex variety $X$, and suppose $X$ has a finite cover by $T$-invariant affine open subvarieties. Use rational coefficients. Let $K=(S^1)^r$ be the maximal compact subgroup of $T$, and use the product right Milnor model $E_K=(E_{S^1})^r$, $B_K=E_K/K=(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^r$. The inclusion $K\subset T$ gives the same topological Borel construction up to homotopy. For each algebraic character $\chi:T\to\mathbb C^\times$, let $L_\chi=E_K\times_K\mathbb C_{\chi|_K}\to B_K$, with right equivalence $(e,z)\cdot t=(e\cdot t,\chi(t)^{-1}z)$, and put $u_\chi=c_1(L_\chi)$. For the coordinate characters $\chi_i$ and $u_i=u_{\chi_i}$, the coefficient ring is $R_T=H^*(B_K;\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q[u_1,\ldots,u_r]$, with $|u_i|=2$ and $u_\chi=\sum_i n_i u_i$ for $\chi(t_1,\ldots,t_r)=\prod_i t_i^{n_i}$. Let $S_T$ be the multiplicative set consisting of $1$ and finite products of $u_\chi$ for nontrivial $\chi$.

Let $H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(X;\mathbb Q)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D^b_{T,c}(X;\mathbb Q)}(\mathbb Q_X,\omega_X^T[-j])$, where $\omega_X^T$ is the normalized equivariant dualizing object whose restriction is the ordinary dualizing object $\omega_X$, without a quotient-stack dimension shift. Equivalently, this is the stable value in degree $j$ of $H^{\mathrm{BM}}_{j+2rm}(X_m;\mathbb Q)$, where $U_m=(\mathbb C^{m+1}\setminus\{0\})^r$ has the free right scalar $T$-action, $X_m=(U_m\times X)/T$ uses $(e,x)\cdot t=(e\cdot t,t^{-1}\cdot x)$, and the supplied bounded-Hom comparison is taken in its stable range. The ring $R_T$ acts by pullback from $B_K$ and cap product. For an $R_T$-module $M$, $S_T^{-1}M$ consists of fractions $m/s$ with $m\in M$, $s\in S_T$, and $m/s=m'/s'$ exactly when some $t\in S_T$ satisfies $t(s'm-sm')=0$; addition and scalar multiplication are the induced fraction operations. Proper equivariant maps induce degree-preserving pushforwards, invariant open inclusions induce Borel–Moore restrictions, and a smooth pure $d$-dimensional complex variety has its complex-oriented fundamental class $[X]_T$ in degree $2d$. For $r=0$, $R_T=\mathbb Q$ and $S_T=\{1\}$.

manifest_declaration.title: Nonzero eigenfunctions annihilate equivariant BM on their nonvanishing loci
manifest_declaration.statement: Let $T=(\mathbb C^\times)^r$ act algebraically on a separated finite-type complex variety $X$ with a finite invariant affine open cover. Let $U$ be one affine chart, let $f\in\mathcal O(U)$ be regular with a nontrivial character $\chi:T\to\mathbb C^\times$, and fix the convention $f(t\cdot x)=\chi(t)f(x)$. If $D(f)=\{x\in U:f(x)\neq0\}$ is nonempty, then the equivariant character class $u_\chi=c_1(L_{\chi|_K})$ acts by zero on every group $H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(D(f);\mathbb Q)$. It also acts by zero on every such group for a further $T$-invariant open subvariety $V\subseteq D(f)$. Consequently $S_T^{-1}H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(D(f);\mathbb Q)=S_T^{-1}H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(V;\mathbb Q)=0$ for all $j$.

manifest_declaration.title: BM concentration from a finite invariant affine atlas
manifest_declaration.statement:
Let $T=(\mathbb C^\times)^r$ act algebraically on a separated finite-type complex variety $X$ that admits a finite cover by $T$-invariant affine open subvarieties. Let $F=X^T$ be the fixed-point subscheme, $i:F\hookrightarrow X$ its closed inclusion, and let $S_T$ be the character multiplicative set in the localized equivariant Borel–Moore definition. Then in every homological degree $j$, proper pushforward induces an isomorphism
$$
i_*:S_T^{-1}H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(F;\mathbb Q)\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }S_T^{-1}H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(X;\mathbb Q).
$$
No compactness of $X$, normality hypothesis, or compact-orbit-type nilpotence hypothesis is required.

manifest_declaration.title: Intrinsic localized pushforward for a proper fixed locus
manifest_declaration.statement:
Let $T=(\mathbb C^\times)^r$ act on a smooth separated finite-type complex variety $X$ with a finite invariant affine open cover. Let $F=X^T$ be proper, $i:F\hookrightarrow X$, $p_F:F\to\mathrm{pt}$, and $S_T$ the character multiplicative set. By the finite-affine-atlas concentration isomorphism, $i_*:S_T^{-1}H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(F;\mathbb Q)\to S_T^{-1}H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(X;\mathbb Q)$ is invertible. Define the intrinsic localized pushforward
$$
p^{\mathrm{loc}}_*:=p_{F*}\circ(i_*)^{-1}:S_T^{-1}H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(X;\mathbb Q)\longrightarrow S_T^{-1}H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(\mathrm{pt};\mathbb Q),
$$
where $p_{F*}$ is the genuine proper Borel–Moore pushforward. For a homogeneous $\alpha\in H_T^q(X;\mathbb Q)$ and smooth complex dimension $d$, an allowed insertion is $\alpha\cap[X]_T\in H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_{2d-q}(X;\mathbb Q)$; the fundamental class $[X]_T$ is the complex-oriented class, not the cohomological unit $1\in H_T^0(X;\mathbb Q)$. This construction does not define an ordinary pushforward along a nonproper map $X\to\mathrm{pt}$.

manifest_declaration.title: Complex structure on an associated bundle by realification
manifest_declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; current readiness is recorded separately.
manifest_declaration.statement:
Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional real Lie group, let $\pi:P\to M$ be a smooth
right principal $H$-bundle, let $W$ be a finite-dimensional complex vector
space, and let $\rho:H\to\mathrm{GL}_{\mathbb C}(W)$ be a smooth complex
representation. Regard $W$ as the underlying real vector space $W_{\mathbb R}$
and $\rho$ as the real representation $\rho_{\mathbb R}$. The associated
quotient $P\times_{H,\rho_{\mathbb R}}W_{\mathbb R}$ has the smooth real
vector-bundle structure supplied by the associated-vector-bundle theorem. The
map $J[p,w]=[p,iw]$ is well-defined and smooth and satisfies $J^2=-\mathrm{id}$.
It therefore gives this real bundle a complex vector-bundle structure of rank
$\dim_{\mathbb C}W$, with transition maps $\rho(g_{ji})$ in any local principal
trivializations $s_i=s_jg_{ji}$. This assertion specifies the complex structure
induced by $J$ and makes no uniqueness claim about other possible complex
structures on the same real bundle.

manifest_declaration.title: Rigid supersymmetric background and localization data
manifest_declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; current readiness is recorded separately.
manifest_declaration.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Let $M$ be a nonempty Hausdorff second-countable smooth four-manifold without boundary, let $g$ be a smooth positive-definite metric on $TM$, and choose an orientation $o$. Coordinates $x^\mu$ have units of length, the metric components in length coordinates are dimensionless, and the scalar curvature has units of inverse length squared. A concrete background may instead have a boundary, but then its boundary conditions and the vanishing or treatment of every boundary term are additional data.

Write $SO(4)=\{R\in M_4(\mathbb R):R^{\mathsf T}R=I,\ \det R=1\}$. For $x\in M$, an oriented $g$-orthonormal frame is an orientation-preserving linear isometry $e:\mathbb R^4\to T_xM$. The oriented orthonormal frame bundle $F_g^+(M)$ is the set of these frames, with projection to $M$ and right action $e\cdot R=e\circ R$. Its smooth principal $SO(4)$-bundle structure is part of the supplied geometry. A Euclidean spin structure is a smooth right principal $\operatorname{Spin}(4)$-bundle $\widetilde F\to M$ and a smooth equivariant map $\lambda:\widetilde F\to F_g^+(M)$ whose restriction to every fibre is a two-sheeted cover. Use $\operatorname{Spin}(4)=SU(2)_+\times SU(2)_-$, where $SU(2)=\left\{\begin{pmatrix}z&w\\-\bar w&\bar z\end{pmatrix}:z,w\in\mathbb C,\ |z|^2+|w|^2=1\right\}$ and the two factors act by their defining matrix representations on $\mathbb C^2$. Identify each factor with the unit quaternions by $\begin{pmatrix}z&w\\-\bar w&\bar z\end{pmatrix}\leftrightarrow z+w\mathbf j$, with $\mathbf j^2=-1$ and $\mathbf j z=\bar z\mathbf j$; write $\mathbb H=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{1,i,\mathbf j,i\mathbf j\}\cong\mathbb R^4$. The fixed standard double-covering homomorphism $\rho:\operatorname{Spin}(4)\to SO(4)$ is $\rho(u_+,u_-)q=u_+qu_-^{-1}$; it is surjective with kernel $\{(1,1),(-1,-1)\}$. The chiral spinor bundles are the associated bundles $S_\pm=\widetilde F\times_{\pi_\pm}\mathbb C^2$, where $\pi_\pm$ are the defining representations of the two $SU(2)$ factors and the quotient convention is $(ps,z)\sim(p,\pi_\pm(s)z)$. Equip each real associated bundle with the complex structure $[p,z]\mapsto[p,iz]$, so $S_\pm$ has complex rank two. A spin connection is a principal connection on $\widetilde F$ projecting to the Levi-Civita connection of $g$; it induces covariant derivatives on $S_\pm$. A spin structure and its connection are supplied data, not conclusions that follow from the metric.

An R-symmetry background consists of a specified finite-dimensional Lie group $K_R$, a smooth right principal $K_R$-bundle $P_R\to M$, a principal connection $A_R$, and a declared smooth representation of $K_R$ on each field bundle. Gauge data consist of a specified compact Lie group $G$, a smooth right principal $G$-bundle $P_G\to M$, its gauge group of smooth bundle automorphisms over $\operatorname{id}_M$, and a principal connection $A$. Matter and auxiliary fields are smooth sections of explicitly declared vector bundles associated to $\widetilde F$, $P_R$, and $P_G$; bosonic and fermionic fields are assigned even and odd parity, respectively. The curvature, global form of $G$, representations, bundle sectors, and reality contours are part of the model data.

A rigid supersymmetric background datum is a fixed Riemannian metric, spin structure and spin connection, R-symmetry background, supergravity auxiliary background fields, and a nonzero smooth spinor section $\epsilon$ in a declared spinor/R-symmetry representation. It also supplies the exact first-order linear system $\mathscr K(\nabla^S,A_R,\mathcal B)(\epsilon)=0$ imposed on $\epsilon$, where $\mathcal B$ denotes the named auxiliary background fields and $\mathscr K$ is the operator obtained by setting the chosen supergravity fermion variation to zero. The equation, its signature, gamma-matrix convention, spinor reality conditions, and boundary conditions must be specified separately for each model; no universal Killing-spinor equation or existence statement is built into this definition. “Rigid” means the metric and supergravity fields are fixed external data and are not integrated over.

An off-shell multiplet is a specified $\mathbb Z_2$-graded collection of bosonic, fermionic, and auxiliary fields together with an odd transformation $Q$ on all of them. An isometry is a diffeomorphism preserving $g$ and $o$; its action on associated bundles must also be supplied. A flavor transformation is the action of a separately named global internal group on the declared field representations. The multiplet closes off shell when $Q^2$ equals an explicitly declared combination of lifted spacetime isometries, gauge transformations, R-symmetry transformations, and flavor transformations on every field, without using Euler–Lagrange equations. A localization package additionally specifies its field configuration space $\mathcal F$, action $S$, gauge group $\mathcal G$, a gauge-fixing slice (a locally transverse condition on gauge orbits), the associated Faddeev–Popov operator and determinant, and a ghost complex (graded ghost, antighost, and multiplier fields with an odd BRST differential). A Faddeev–Popov zero mode is a vector in the kernel of the specified gauge-fixing operator; stabilizer modes are infinitesimal gauge transformations that fix the chosen connection. The package also specifies its integration contour $\mathcal C$, boundary conditions, and either an actual measure or a regulator map from field configurations to regulated spaces $\mathcal F_\Lambda$ with measures $\mu_\Lambda$. If a measure is only written formally as $[D\Phi]$, this notation is not a constructed measure. Applying a $Q$-exact deformation $S_t=S+tQV$ further requires an explicit assumption or proof of $Q$-invariance of the regulated measure and contour, absence or treatment of anomalies, justified differentiation under the integral, and vanishing or controlled boundary terms. This definition supplies no such proof.

For a four-dimensional gauge model in these units, $g_{\mathrm{YM}}$ is dimensionless, $[A_\mu]=[\Phi]=\mathrm{length}^{-1}$, $[F_{\mu\nu}]=\mathrm{length}^{-2}$, and a fermion field has mass dimension $3/2$; the supercharge has mass dimension $1/2$ and its spinor parameter has mass dimension $-1/2$. Every additional mass, radius, equivariant parameter, and suppressed constant must be assigned dimensions in the concrete item. No metric is asserted to admit this data, and finite-dimensional equivariant identities alone do not construct a continuum field-space measure.

manifest_declaration.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. For $r>0$, let

$$S^4_r=\{y\in\mathbb R^5:\sum_{j=1}^5 y_j^2=r^2\}$$

with its standard orientation, round metric, scalar curvature $12/r^2$, and standard spin structure. In stereographic length coordinates $x^\mu$, $\mu=1,\ldots,4$, use

$$ds^2=\frac{\sum_{\mu=1}^4 (dx^\mu)^2}{(1+x^2/(4r^2))^2},\qquad x^2=\sum_{\mu=1}^4(x^\mu)^2.$$

Let $G=U(2)$, with Lie algebra $\mathfrak u(2)=\{X\in M_2(\mathbb C):X^\dagger=-X\}$ and positive invariant form $(X,Y)=-\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf 2}(XY)$. A gauge sector is a smooth right principal $U(2)$ bundle $P\to S^4_r$ up to smooth bundle isomorphism, with a smooth connection $A$ and curvature $F_A=dA+A\wedge A$ in a local trivialization. Fields in the adjoint representation are sections of the associated adjoint bundle. This postulate does not classify the bundle sectors. 

The microscopic field content is one four-dimensional rigid $\mathcal N=2$ vector multiplet and one adjoint hypermultiplet: the vector multiplet has the connection, one complex adjoint scalar, two adjoint Weyl fermions, and an $SU(2)_R$ auxiliary triplet; the hypermultiplet has two complex adjoint scalars and one adjoint Dirac fermion. There is no other matter. 

The hypermultiplet has real Euclidean mass $m_E$ of mass dimension one, supplied by a background flavor-vector multiplet. 

In the source's orthonormal basis for its four scalar directions, write its mass matrix as $M_{ij}=i m_EJ_{ij}$, where $J$ is the fixed real antisymmetric self-dual complex structure with $J^2=-I$ and source normalization $J_{ij}J^{ij}=4$. This is the $\mathcal N=2^*$ model; $m_E=0$ is its $\mathcal N=4$ limit. 

Adopt the source's Euclidean curvature-coupled action and Scherk–Schwarz mass deformation, with gauge kinetic normalization

$$S_{\mathrm{YM}}=\frac{1}{2g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2} \int_{S^4_r}d^4x\sqrt g\,(F_{\mu\nu},F^{\mu\nu}),$$

where $g_{\mathrm{YM}}>0$ is dimensionless and the trace is in the defining representation. 

The theta angle $\theta$ is real and dimensionless. Set

The selected off-shell supercharge $Q$ uses the source's seven auxiliary scalars and transformations (2.26)–(2.30). With $v^\mu=\epsilon\Gamma^\mu\epsilon$, its square on the vector multiplet is the lifted symmetry

$$Q^2=-\mathcal L_v-\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(v^M A_M)-\delta_R-\delta_\Omega,$$

 where $\mathcal L_v$ is the lifted Lie derivative, $\delta_R$ is the rotation generated by $R_{AB}=2\widetilde\epsilon\widetilde\Gamma_{AB} \epsilon$, and $\delta_\Omega$ is the dilation proportional to $2\widetilde\epsilon\epsilon=0$. The source adds constant variables $\widetilde a_0,b_0,c_0,\widetilde c_0$ to handle the zero-mode sector and uses $Q=s+\delta$; its square is the constant gauge transformation together with the selected $U(1)$ rotation. Adopt independently a rigid four-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ pure Yang–Mills model on oriented and time-oriented $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$, $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, with increasing $x^0$ time orientation and natural units $c=\hbar=1$. The global group is $SU(2)$, with one supplied smooth right principal bundle $P\to M$ and smooth equivariant local trivializations. The connection and its curvature are $A$ and $F_A=dA+\tfrac12[A\wedge A]$, in the right-action convention of the Yang–Mills model supplier. Use anti-Hermitian $T_a=-i\sigma_a/2$ and $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}(XY)$; let $\kappa_{\mathbb C}$ be its complex-bilinear extension and $\kappa_H(\bar X,Y)=\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\bar X,Y)$. Fix $g>0$ dimensionless and theta angle zero. A bundle sector means its smooth equivariant isomorphism class over $M$; only the supplied sector is used.

The microscopic matter-hypermultiplet index set is empty. The vector multiplet comprises the connection, one complex adjoint scalar $\phi$, and two adjoint left-Weyl fermions. In $\mathcal N=1$ packaging it is a real adjoint vector superfield $V$ and an adjoint chiral superfield $\Phi$, not a matter hypermultiplet. Use the supplied superspace derivatives, chirality, ordered Berezin measures and vector-supergauge convention, including

$$\mathcal C_{\alpha,R}=-\tfrac14\bar D^2(e^{-2gV_R}D_\alpha e^{2gV_R}),\qquad [X]_D=-\tfrac14 I_D(X),\qquad [Y]_F=\tfrac12 I_F(Y).$$

Here $\mathcal C_{\alpha,R}$ is the represented matrix curvature, not the abstract Lie-algebra curvature used in the action. With Hermitian $t_{a,R}=i\rho_{R*}(T_a)$, let $W_{\mathrm{can},\alpha}^a$ denote the canonically normalized component field-strength superfields, so $\mathcal C_{\alpha,R}=2g\,t_{a,R}W_{\mathrm{can},\alpha}^a$. Define the abstract connection-normalized curvature by

$$\mathcal W_{\mathrm{conn},\alpha}=gT_aW_{\mathrm{can},\alpha}^a,\qquad \rho_{R*}(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{conn},\alpha})=\frac{\mathcal C_{\alpha,R}}{2i}.$$

In the fundamental representation, $\kappa_{\mathbb C}=-2\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}$ therefore gives $\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{conn}}^\alpha,\mathcal W_{\mathrm{conn},\alpha})=\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}(\mathcal C^\alpha\mathcal C_\alpha)$, with the same ordered spinor product on both sides. This is a classical representation/component normalization, not a quantum field-rescaling or threshold-matching theorem.

Adopt the connection-normalized microscopic action

$$S_{\mathrm{pure}}=\int_M d^4x\left\{\frac1{g^2}[\kappa_H(\bar\Phi,e^{2gV_{\mathrm{ad}}}\Phi)]_D+\left(\left[\frac1{4g^2}\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{conn}}^\alpha,\mathcal W_{\mathrm{conn},\alpha})\right]_F+\mathrm{h.c.}\right)\right\}.$$

Here $I_D,I_F$ are the raw ordered mathematical integrals, and the physical action brackets and chiral components use def-qftx-physical-superspace-normalization. The Hermitian-conjugate operation applies only to the chiral F term; the D term is real. Equivalently, the fundamental matrix F integrand is $\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}(\mathcal C^\alpha\mathcal C_\alpha)/(8g^2)$, plus its Hermitian conjugate. Its bosonic gauge density is fixed to $-\kappa(F_A\wedge *_\eta F_A)/(2g^2)$. There is no chiral superpotential, hypermultiplet, hypermultiplet mass, or FI parameter in this ultraviolet datum. The scalar is connection-normalized; its canonical version is $\phi_{\mathrm{can}}=\phi/g$. In the same local Berezin normalization the quadratic microscopic prepotential is $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{UV}}(\Phi)=i\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\Phi,\Phi)/(2g^2)$, with positive imaginary Hessian $\kappa/g^2$. The prepotential has mass dimension two. The dimensions are $[x]=-1$, $[\theta]=-1/2$, $[A]=[\phi]=1$, $[F_A]=2$, $[\mathcal W_{\mathrm{conn}}]=[\mathcal C]=3/2$, and $[g]=0$.

Eight real rigid supercharges, their $\mathcal N=2$ algebra and invariance of this adopted action are model premises, not a locally proved invariance theorem. Variations are smooth and compactly supported; actions are on relatively compact regions or where integrable. A small $\mathcal N=1$ adjoint-mass perturbation and the Seiberg–Witten solution are separate subsequent inputs. In particular an emergent infrared monopole hypermultiplet is not microscopic matter added to this pure model. This postulate defines classical ultraviolet field/action data; it constructs no quantum measure, regulator limit, interacting continuum theory, or empirical verification.
