manifest_declaration.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ and Minkowski signature $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-,+,+,+)$. Take QED with a real one-form photon potential $A=A_\mu dx^\mu$ on $\mathbb R^{1,3}$, field strength $F=dA$ with components $F_{\mu
u}=\partial_\mu A_
u-\partial_
u A_\mu$, and two Dirac fields $\psi_e,\psi_\mu$, each a four-component complex spinor-valued field, of charge $-e$ and positive masses $m_e<M_\mu$. Use the minimal-coupling convention $D_\mu=\partial_\mu+ieA_\mu$ for charge $-e$, and the gauge kinetic term $-	frac14F_{\mu
u}F^{\mu
u}$. Define the dimensionless running coupling by $\alpha_{\mathrm{DS}}(\mu)=e_{\mathrm{DS}}(\mu)^2/(4\pi)$. The decoupling-subtraction (DS) convention uses minimal subtraction within each interval of active charged fields, removes a charged field from the low-energy theory below its threshold, and matches the coupling continuously at that threshold. Set $\alpha_{\mathrm{DS}}(m_e)=\alpha_{\mathrm{phys}}>0$ as the low-energy boundary condition. The source-reported one-loop DS flow has two active Dirac fields for $\mu>M_\mu$, one for $m_e<\mu<M_\mu$, and none for $\mu<m_e$. If the one-loop solution remains in its positive-coupling domain, then for positive evaluation scale $Q$ of mass dimension one,
$$ rac{1}{\alpha_{\mathrm{DS}}(Q)}= rac{1}{\alpha_{\mathrm{phys}}}- rac{1}{3\pi}\log\!\left( rac{Q^2}{m_e^2}ight)\qquad(m_e<Q<M_\mu),$$
and
$$ rac{1}{\alpha_{\mathrm{DS}}(Q)}= rac{1}{\alpha_{\mathrm{phys}}}- rac{1}{3\pi}\log\!\left( rac{M_\mu^2}{m_e^2}ight)- rac{2}{3\pi}\log\!\left( rac{Q^2}{M_\mu^2}ight)\qquad(Q>M_\mu).$$
The two expressions agree continuously at $Q=M_\mu$. These are solutions of the supplied one-loop renormalization-group equations; they are not measured values, exact all-orders predictions, or numerical error estimates.

manifest_declaration.title: Leading Wilsonian Superpotential Match at a Supersymmetric Chiral Threshold
manifest_declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; planned item contract; readiness recorded separately.
manifest_declaration.statement:
Assume full Axiom of Choice for the selected finite operator-equivalence data. Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ and the rigid four-dimensional $\mathcal N=1$ Wilsonian EFT data in the action definition. Let $\Phi$ be a finite collection of light chiral superfields and let $X$ be one heavy gauge-singlet chiral superfield with canonical physical D-term $[X^\dagger X]_D$. Suppose the derivative-free holomorphic high-energy superpotential is

$$W_+(\Phi,X)=W_L(\Phi)+\frac12 M X^2+XJ(\Phi),$$

where $M>0$ has mass dimension one, $[\Phi_i]=[X]=1$, $W_L$ is a gauge-invariant holomorphic function of mass dimension three, and $J$ is a gauge-singlet holomorphic function of mass dimension two. The model identifies the physical heavy threshold mass with this positive coefficient $M$. Let $\Pi_0$ denote the projection in the supplied formal superspace-derivative expansion onto degree zero in $\partial_\mu,D_\alpha,\bar D_{\dot\alpha}$, with each $D$ and $\bar D$ assigned degree $1/2$; this is a formal truncation and gives no numerical remainder bound. Assume the declared tree-level threshold prescription uses the $\Pi_0$ projection of the full chiral equation obtained by varying the canonical $X^\dagger X$ term and $W_+$, at external energies $E_{\mathrm{ext}}\ll M$, with a fixed finite operator basis and truncation. Then the holomorphic coefficient component of this tree-level Wilsonian threshold map is

$$W_-^{(0)}(\Phi)=W_L(\Phi)-\frac{J(\Phi)^2}{2M}.$$

The Wilsonian scale $\mu_W$, renormalization scale $\mu$, $M$, $E_{\mathrm{ext}}$, regulator cutoff $\Lambda_{\mathrm{reg}}$, and operator-suppression scale $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}$ remain distinct inputs; no equality among them is inferred. This result gives the leading derivative-free F-term coordinate only. The matching definition's equality for selected renormalized amplitudes or Green functions, its common infrared regulator, and its retained truncation must still be checked as supplied matching data. No loop, arbitrary one-particle-irreducible, nonperturbative, or continuum statement follows.

manifest_declaration.statement:
Let the rigid four-dimensional $\mathcal N=1$ Wilsonian effective-action data and finite operator basis be as in the action definition, with formal cutoff $0<\lambda<\Lambda_0$. Let $F_\lambda(\Phi,W)$ denote the derivative-free, holomorphic chiral integrand of the Wilsonian action, and define its superpotential part by $W_\lambda(\Phi)=F_\lambda(\Phi,0)$. Fix a finite ordered basis of retained light-field superpotential operators and a scale-independent linear coordinate projection $P_{\mathrm{hol}}$ onto that basis. Use the same unrescaled chiral fields, quotient relations, and operator coordinates at every scale. Assume the selected formal perturbative cutoff prescription has the local nondynamical-spurion extension and local derivative expansion specified in the action data; its perturbative vertices are one-particle-irreducible; its rigid supersymmetry and BRST/gauge Ward identities hold coefficientwise for every local insertion and their counterterms; and it has no local gauge anomaly.

Assume full Axiom of Choice for the selected finite operator-equivalence data. Then, coefficientwise at every perturbative order,

$$P_{\mathrm{hol}}W_\lambda=P_{\mathrm{hol}}W_{\Lambda_0}.$$

Thus every retained holomorphic superpotential coefficient in the fixed unrescaled field basis is unchanged by the formal Wilsonian cutoff evolution. The separately displayed holomorphic gauge coupling may receive a one-loop correction but no higher-loop correction. The real D-term function and Kähler data may change. This does not constrain arbitrary one-particle-irreducible vertices, coefficients after a scale-dependent field rescaling, nonperturbative corrections, or a continuum interacting quantum field theory.

manifest_declaration.title: Heavy-Chiral Threshold and a Spurion Soft Trilinear
manifest_declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; planned item contract; readiness recorded separately.
manifest_declaration.statement:
Take one light gauge-singlet chiral superfield $\Phi$ and one heavy gauge-singlet chiral superfield $X$, with canonical quadratic D-terms, in the rigid flat-space $\mathcal N=1$ convention of the Wilsonian action definition. Let $M>0$ be the heavy threshold mass, let $g,y,\kappa\in\mathbb C$ be dimensionless, and choose

$$W_+(\Phi,X)=\frac12MX^2+\frac g2X\Phi^2+\frac y6\Phi^3.$$

Use the tree-level zero-supercovariant-derivative matching prescription at external energies $E_{\mathrm{ext}}\ll M$. The matched holomorphic Wilsonian superpotential coefficient is

$$W_-(\Phi)=\frac y6\Phi^3-\frac{g^2}{8M}\Phi^4.$$

In the low-energy EFT, choose a fixed nondynamical chiral spurion background $\mathcal X=2\theta^1\theta^2 F_{\mathcal X}$ with $[\mathcal X]=1$ and constant $[F_{\mathcal X}]=2$, and add the single local operator

$$\Delta W=\frac{\kappa}{6\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}}\mathcal X\Phi^3,$$

where $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}>0$ is an operator-suppression scale distinct from $M$. After fixing this background, the added component term is $\frac{A_{\mathrm{soft}}}{6}\phi^3+\mathrm{h.c.}$ with $A_{\mathrm{soft}}=\kappa F_{\mathcal X}/\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}$ and mass dimension one. Here a soft scalar trilinear means a scalar cubic interaction with a positive-mass-dimension coefficient. This is an explicit spurion insertion, not an observed value or a consequence of the supersymmetric threshold theorem. No numerical smallness bound on $A_{\mathrm{soft}}$ is asserted; omitting additional spurion insertions requires separate power-counting input.

manifest_declaration.title: Finite-Dimensional Q-Exact Deformation Invariance
manifest_declaration.statement:
Let $M$ be an oriented smooth manifold of finite dimension $n$, with integration cycle $M$, smooth positive volume form $\mu$, graded algebra $\mathcal A=\Omega^\bullet(M;\mathbb C)$, and integral $I_\Gamma(F)=\int_M F_{[n]}$ of the degree-$n$ part. Let $Q$ be a smooth odd derivation of $\mathcal A$, let $S,O$ be smooth even forms, let $V$ be a smooth odd form, and let $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval. Suppose $QS=QO=0$, $(Q^2V)e^{-S-tQV}=0$ for every $t\in J$, and $I_\Gamma(Q(O V e^{-S-tQV}))=0$ for every $t\in J$, including the zero-boundary-flux condition. Write $(Oe^{-S-tQV})_{[n]}=f_t\mu$. Suppose that $f_t$ is integrable for each $t\in J$, is differentiable in $t$ almost everywhere with measurable derivative, and that for every compact $K\subset J$ one integrable majorant $g_K$ bounds both $|f_t|$ and $|\partial_t f_t|$ for all $t\in K$, outside one null set. Then

$$Z(t):=I_\Gamma(Oe^{-S-tQV})=\int_M f_t\,d\mu$$

is constant on $J$, and for every $t\in J$,

$$Z'(t)=-I_\Gamma(O(QV)e^{-S-tQV})=-I_\Gamma(Q(O V e^{-S-tQV}))=0.$$

In particular, the conclusion is finite-dimensional and applies only at finite parameter values in $J$; it gives no $t\to\infty$ saddle-point limit and no identity for an infinite-dimensional continuum functional integral.

manifest_declaration.title: The positive-FI and zero-FI rank-one chambers
manifest_declaration.statement: Take $N=k=1$. For every $\zeta>0$, the positive real-FI ADHM quotient is $\mathbb C^2$, with arbitrary scalar coordinates $B_1,B_2$, $J=0$, and $|I|=\sqrt{\zeta}$. The stable zero-real-FI locus is empty. The positive-FI monad is therefore a rank-one framed torsion-free sheaf that is not locally free. On the round oriented $S^4$, let $f$ be the real curvature two-form of a smooth $U(1)$ connection, define anti-self-dual (ASD) by $f=-*f$, and define charge by $q=-(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int_{S^4}f\wedge f$. The ordinary smooth charge-one $U(1)$ ASD space is empty, so the positive-FI space cannot equal it.

manifest_declaration.title: Gauge stabilizers and properness of the Sobolev action
manifest_declaration.design_state: Draft authored for Sobolev and Smooth Gauge-Orbit Geometry; full statement, dependencies, and source qualifications are in the item carrier.
manifest_declaration.statement:
Assume the configuration data and integer $k>d/2+1$ from the preceding definition, and let $\mathcal A_k^*$ be the locus where the holonomy representation on $\mathbb C^N$ is irreducible. For any $A\in\mathcal A_k$, evaluation at $p_m$ identifies its stabilizer in $\mathcal G_{k+1}$ with the centralizer of $\operatorname{Hol}_{p_m}(A)$ in $SU(N)$. Thus an irreducible connection has stabilizer exactly $Z_N$, and the induced action of $\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}=\mathcal G_{k+1}/Z_N$ on $\mathcal A_k^*$ is free. The subset $\mathcal A_k^*$ is open in $\mathcal A_k$.

The Sobolev action is proper: if $A_j\to A$ and $A_j^{u_j}\to B$ in $H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ for sequences $A_j,A,B\in\mathcal A_k$ and $u_j\in\mathcal G_{k+1}$, then some subsequence $u_{j_\ell}$ converges in $H^{k+1}(\operatorname{Ad}P)$ to $u\in\mathcal G_{k+1}$ and $B=A^u$. Equivalently, the action map $\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}\times\mathcal A_k^*\to\mathcal A_k^*\times\mathcal A_k^*$ is proper, meaning inverse images of compact sets are compact.

manifest_declaration.title: Rough-coefficient covariant Green inverse and Coulomb splitting
manifest_declaration.design_state: Draft authored for Sobolev and Smooth Gauge-Orbit Geometry; full statement, dependencies, and source qualifications are in the item carrier.
manifest_declaration.statement:
Assume the configuration data and integer $k>d/2+1$ from the first definition, and let $A\in\mathcal A_k^*$. Define the covariant Laplacian on adjoint sections by

$$\Delta_A:=d_A^*d_A:H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)\longrightarrow H^{k-1}(\operatorname{ad}P).$$

Then $\Delta_A$ is a bounded isomorphism with bounded inverse $G_A:H^{k-1}(\operatorname{ad}P)\to H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)$. Moreover,

$$H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)=\operatorname{im}d_A\oplus\ker d_A^*,$$

and the bounded projection onto $\operatorname{im}d_A$ is $\Pi_A=d_AG_Ad_A^*$. In operator-norm neighborhoods of each irreducible $A$, the inverse $G_A$ and projection $\Pi_A$ depend smoothly on $A$. The imported smooth-coefficient Green theorem is used only for a smooth reference connection; the asserted operator $\Delta_A$ itself may have Sobolev coefficients.

manifest_declaration.title: Sobolev and smooth irreducible gauge-orbit principal bundles
manifest_declaration.design_state: Draft authored for Sobolev and Smooth Gauge-Orbit Geometry; full statement, dependencies, and source qualifications are in the item carrier.
manifest_declaration.statement:
Assume the configuration data and integer $k>d/2+1$ from the first definition. The irreducible locus $\mathcal A_k^*$ is open, and the orbit projection

$$\pi_k:\mathcal A_k^*\longrightarrow \mathcal A_k^*/\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}$$

is a locally trivial smooth principal Banach Lie group bundle. For every $A\in\mathcal A_k^*$ there is an $\varepsilon>0$ such that the Coulomb slice

$$S_{A,\varepsilon}:=\{A+a:a\in\ker d_A^*,\ \|a\|_{H^k}<\varepsilon\}$$

lies in $\mathcal A_k^*$, meets each orbit in its saturation exactly once, and has open saturation. The map $S_{A,\varepsilon}\to\pi_k(S_{A,\varepsilon})$ is a smooth chart of the quotient, whose quotient topology is Hausdorff.

For the $C^\infty$ connection and gauge spaces with the section topologies specified in the first definition, the irreducible projection

$$\pi_\infty:\mathcal A_\infty^*\longrightarrow\mathcal A_\infty^*/\bar{\mathcal G}_\infty$$

is a locally trivial topological principal $\bar{\mathcal G}_\infty$-bundle with the actual $C^\infty$ quotient topology. No inverse-limit assertion alone is used to obtain this smooth-space conclusion.

manifest_declaration.title: Coulomb chart linearization and derivative loss
manifest_declaration.design_state: Draft authored for Sobolev and Smooth Gauge-Orbit Geometry — Examples; full statement, dependencies, and source qualifications are in the item carrier.
manifest_declaration.statement:
Let $A\in\mathcal A_k^*$ for the configuration data and integer $k>d/2+1$. The differential at $(0,0)$ of the Coulomb-gauge action map

$$\Phi_A:\ker(d_A^*:H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)\to H^{k-1}(\operatorname{ad}P))\times H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)\longrightarrow\mathcal A_k,\qquad (a,\xi)\longmapsto(A+a)^{\exp\xi},$$

is the bounded isomorphism

$$L_A(a,\xi)=a+d_A\xi.$$

Its inverse, for $v\in H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$, is

$$L_A^{-1}v=\bigl(v-d_AG_Ad_A^*v,\ G_Ad_A^*v\bigr),$$

where $G_A=(d_A^*d_A)^{-1}:H^{k-1}(\operatorname{ad}P)\to H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)$. Thus the connection variation lies in $H^k$, the infinitesimal gauge parameter lies in $H^{k+1}$, and the gauge term $d_A\xi$ loses one derivative. This is a linearized chart statement and asserts no determinant or measure formula.

manifest_declaration.title: Central stabilizer and based stabilizer comparison
manifest_declaration.design_state: Draft authored for Sobolev and Smooth Gauge-Orbit Geometry — Examples; full statement, dependencies, and source qualifications are in the item carrier.
manifest_declaration.statement: Let $M$ be compact and connected, let $P\to M$ be a smooth right principal $SU(N)$-bundle with a fixed basepoint lift $p_m$, and let $A$ be a smooth connection with integer regularity index $k>d/2+1$. The evaluation map $u\mapsto u(p_m)$ identifies the stabilizer $\{u\in\mathcal G_{k+1}:A^u=A\}$ with the centralizer $C_{SU(N)}(\operatorname{Hol}_{p_m}(A))$. Consequently the based stabilizer inside $\mathcal G_{k+1,m}:=\{u:u(p_m)=e\}$ is trivial for every $A$. If $A$ is irreducible on $\mathbb C^N$, its full stabilizer is $Z_N=\{zI_N:z^N=1\}$, so its stabilizer under the reduced group $\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}=\mathcal G_{k+1}/Z_N$ is trivial as well.

manifest_declaration.title: Compact coherent cohomology can be finite and nonzero
manifest_declaration.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $P^1(\mathbb C)$ have standard charts $U_0=\{Z_0\ne0\}$ and $U_1=\{Z_1\ne0\}$, with coordinates $z=Z_1/Z_0$ on $U_0\cong\mathbb C$ and $w=Z_0/Z_1=1/z$ on $U_1\cong\mathbb C$. Let $\mathcal O(-2)$ be the projective twisting line bundle with local frames satisfying $e_1=z^{-2}e_0$ on $U_0\cap U_1\cong\mathbb C^*$. Then
$$
H^1(P^1(\mathbb C),\mathcal O(-2))\cong\mathbb C.
$$
Thus finite-dimensionality of compact coherent cohomology does not imply vanishing of positive-degree cohomology.

manifest_declaration.title: Finite-support coherent sheaves have only finitely many sections
manifest_declaration.statement: Assume full AC. Let $0\le r\le3$ and let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent analytic module on $P^r(\mathbb C)$ whose support $S:=\{x\in P^r(\mathbb C):\mathcal F_x\ne0\}$ is finite. Assume each stalk $\mathcal F_x$ is finite-dimensional over $\mathbb C$, and put $\ell:=\sum_{x\in S}\dim_{\mathbb C}\mathcal F_x$. Then $H^0(P^r(\mathbb C),\mathcal F)\cong\bigoplus_{x\in S}\mathcal F_x$ has complex dimension $\ell$, and $H^q(P^r(\mathbb C),\mathcal F)=0$ for every $q>0$. Here $H^q$ is ordinary right-derived sheaf cohomology and $\ell$ is the total complex length of the finite-support sheaf.
manifest_declaration.strategy: Decompose finite-support data into skyscraper sheaves and compute their cohomology.

manifest_declaration.title: A coherent point quotient and its first syzygies
manifest_declaration.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $N\ge1$, let $D\subset\mathbb C^N$ be a polydisc centered at the origin with coordinates $z_1,\ldots,z_N$, and let $\mathcal F$ be the cokernel sheaf of $\mu:\mathcal O_D^{\oplus N}\to\mathcal O_D$, $\mu(a_1,\ldots,a_N)=\sum_{i=1}^N a_i z_i$. The stalk of $\mathcal F$ is $\mathbb C$ at the origin and zero at every other point of $D$. The sheaf $\mathcal F$ is coherent, and the kernel of $\mu$ is generated on $D$ by the coordinate Koszul sections $z_j e_i-z_i e_j$ for $1\le i<j\le N$; for $N=1$ this generating family is empty.

manifest_declaration.title: A noncompact variety with a proper fixed component
manifest_declaration.statement: Let $T=\mathbb C^\times$ act on $X=\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb C$ by $t\cdot([x:y],z)=([x:y],tz)$, and give $X$ the two invariant affine charts $\{x\neq0\}\times\mathbb C$ and $\{y\neq0\}\times\mathbb C$. Its fixed locus is the proper component $F=\mathbb P^1\times\{0\}$, although $X$ is noncompact. Let $\chi(t)=t$, $u=c_1(L_{\chi|_{S^1}})$, choose $p\in\mathbb P^1$, and let $h\in H^2(\mathbb P^1;\mathbb Q)$ be the complex-oriented Gysin class of $p$, so $\int_{\mathbb P^1}h=1$. Pull $h$ back to $\alpha\in H_T^2(X;\mathbb Q)$ by the projection $X\to\mathbb P^1$. Compute the intrinsic localized pushforward of $\alpha\cap[X]_T$; it is $1/u$.

manifest_declaration.title: Taubes disk barriers and monotone Dirichlet iteration
manifest_declaration.statement:
Let $\kappa>0$ and let $D=\sum_{j=1}^Jm_j[z_j]$ be a finite effective divisor in $\mathbb C$, where the centers $z_j$ are distinct and $m_j\in\mathbb N$; write $N=\sum_jm_j$. For any $a>0$ with $a\ge4N/\kappa$, the function
$$u_-(z)=\sum_{j=1}^Jm_j\log\frac{|z-z_j|^2}{|z-z_j|^2+a}$$
is a global distributional subsolution of $\Delta u+\kappa(1-e^u)=4\pi\sum_jm_j\delta_{z_j}$. For every $R>\max_j|z_j|$ (with the empty maximum interpreted as $0$), let $D_R=\{|z|<R\}$ and define
$$u_{s,R}(z)=\sum_jm_j\log\frac{R^2|z-z_j|^2}{|R^2-\overline z_jz|^2},\qquad \psi_R(z)=\frac{\kappa}{4}(R^2-|z|^2),\qquad A_R=e^{u_{s,R}}.$$
Then $u_{s,R}$ is the zero-boundary Dirichlet Green sum with $\Delta u_{s,R}=4\pi\sum_jm_j\delta_{z_j}$; $u_{s,R}+\psi_R$ is a supersolution and $u_-\le u_{s,R}+\psi_R$ on $D_R$. Write $H^1_0(D_R;\mathbb R)$ for the closure of $C_c^\infty(D_R;\mathbb R)$ in the real Sobolev space $W^{1,2}(D_R;\mathbb R)$. For any constant $L_R\ge\kappa\max_{\overline D_R}(A_Re^{\psi_R})$, the positive zero-Dirichlet resolver $(-\Delta+L_R)^{-1}$ on $H^1_0(D_R;\mathbb R)$ defines the monotone iteration
$$v_0=u_--u_{s,R},\qquad v_{k+1}=(-\Delta+L_R)^{-1}\bigl(\kappa+L_Rv_k-\kappa A_Re^{v_k}\bigr).$$
It converges pointwise and in $H^1(D_R)$ to a solution $v_R\in C^{2,\alpha}(\overline D_R)$ for every $0<\alpha<1$, with $v_0\le v_R\le\psi_R$ and zero boundary trace. Thus $u_R=u_{s,R}+v_R$ solves the distributional divisor equation, satisfies $u_-\le u_R\le0$, and has $u_R-2\sum_jm_j\log|z-z_j|$ smooth at the centers. For the fixed singular function $s(z)=2\sum_jm_j\log|z-z_j|$, every compact $K\subset\mathbb C$ and every $p>2$ admit constants independent of sufficiently large $R$ such that $u_R-s$ is uniformly bounded in $W^{2,p}(K)$. For each $0<\alpha<1$, choosing $p>2/(1-\alpha)$ also gives a uniform $C^{2,\alpha}(K)$ bound. These are the local compactness estimates for disk exhaustion.

Choose L>=kappa max A_R exp(psi); (-Delta+L) inverse positive by maximum principle. Iterate T(v)=(-Delta+L)^-1[kappa+Lv-kappa A_R exp(v)] between lower u_minus-u_sing and upper psi. manifest_declaration.title: Planar critical vortices for arbitrary finite divisors
manifest_declaration.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix $e>0$, $\xi>0$, $\kappa=2e^2\xi$, and an effective finite divisor $D=\sum_{j=1}^Jm_j[z_j]$ on $\mathbb C$ with distinct centers and positive integer multiplicities; let $N=\sum_jm_j$. There is a unique real scalar function $h$, smooth on $\mathbb C\setminus\{z_j\}$, such that $h-2m_j\log|z-z_j|$ extends smoothly across each center, $h\to0$ as $|z|\to\infty$, and
$$\Delta h+\kappa(1-e^h)=4\pi\sum_{j=1}^Jm_j\delta_{z_j}$$
in distributions, where $\langle\delta_z,\psi\rangle=\psi(z)$ for $\psi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2)$. For $N>0$, $h<0$ off the divisor; for the empty divisor, $h=0$. With $P(z)=\prod_j(z-z_j)^{m_j}$, $s=2\log|P|$, and the orientation $*dx_1=dx_2$, $*dx_2=-dx_1$, the fields
$$q(z)=\sqrt\xi\,e^{(h(z)-s(z))/2}P(z),\qquad A=-\tfrac12 *d(h-s)$$
extend smoothly across the centers and solve $(D_{A,1}+iD_{A,2})q=0$ and $B=e^2(\xi-|q|^2)$, where $D_A=d-iA$ and $B\,dx_1\wedge dx_2=dA$. They have finite energy
$$E(A,q)=\int_{\mathbb R^2}\left(\frac{B^2}{2e^2}+|D_{A,1}q|^2+|D_{A,2}q|^2+\frac{e^2}{2}(|q|^2-\xi)^2\right)dx_1dx_2$$
and flux $\int_{\mathbb R^2}B\,dx_1dx_2=2\pi N$. For every $0<\alpha<\sqrt\kappa$ and every multi-index $\beta$, $|\partial^\beta h(z)|=O(e^{-\alpha|z|})$ as $|z|\to\infty$; the curvature $B$ and covariant gradient $D_Aq$ have the same exponential decay. On the exterior of a disk, the local gauge $e^{-i\arg P}$ gives $q_{\mathrm{ext}}=\sqrt\xi e^{h/2}$ and $A_{\mathrm{ext}}=-\tfrac12 *dh$, so the fields approach the vacuum exponentially in that exterior gauge; the raw global representative $q$ need not have an exponentially small phase correction. Negative winding $-N$ is obtained by complex conjugation and $A\mapsto-A$, with flux $-2\pi N$.

manifest_declaration.title: Global energy minima for critical Abelian Higgs vortices
manifest_declaration.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix $e>0$ and $\xi>0$ and use the critical Abelian-Higgs energy and boundary-sector convention in which $D_A=d-iA$, $B=dA$, $q$ tends in modulus to $\sqrt\xi$, and its exterior phase has winding $n\in\mathbb Z$. For every smooth finite-energy field pair $(A,q)$ in that sector,
$$E(A,q)\ge 2\pi\xi|n|.$$
For $n\ge0$, the exact identity is
$$E(A,q)=\int_{\mathbb R^2}\left(|(D_{A,1}+iD_{A,2})q|^2+\frac{(B-e^2(\xi-|q|^2))^2}{2e^2}\right)dx_1dx_2+2\pi\xi n;$$
for $n\le0$, replace $D_{A,1}+iD_{A,2}$ by $D_{A,1}-iD_{A,2}$ and $B-e^2(\xi-|q|^2)$ by $B+e^2(\xi-|q|^2)$, with topological term $-2\pi\xi n$. The boundary-current term in the disk identity vanishes along a radius sequence derived from the finite-energy hypotheses. The fields reconstructed for any fixed divisor by the arbitrary-divisor plane theorem attain equality, are absolute transverse energy minima in their winding sector, have zero first variation under smooth compactly supported variations, and have nonnegative second variation in those directions. This does not assert uniqueness of minimizing fields across distinct divisors of the same degree.

manifest_declaration.title: Fixed-flux cylinders and uniform end-collar energy
manifest_declaration.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix $e>0$, $\xi>0$, $\kappa=2e^2\xi$, and $n\in\mathbb Z$. For transverse fields on the oriented Euclidean plane, let $A_\perp=A_1dx_1+A_2dx_2$ be a smooth real one-form, let $q:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb C$ be smooth, set $D_iq=(\partial_i-iA_i)q$ and $B_{12}=\partial_1A_2-\partial_2A_1$, and define
$$E_\perp(A_\perp,q)=\int_{\mathbb R^2}\left(\frac{B_{12}^2}{2e^2}+|D_1q|^2+|D_2q|^2+\frac{e^2}{2}(|q|^2-\xi)^2\right)dx_1dx_2.$$
For $L>0$, write $\Omega_L=\mathbb R^2\times[0,L]$ with coordinates $(x_1,x_2,z)$, let $\mathcal A=A_1dx_1+A_2dx_2+A_3dz$ be a smooth real connection one-form, let $q:\Omega_L\to\mathbb C$ be smooth up to the ends, set $F=d\mathcal A$, $D_\mu q=(\partial_\mu-iA_\mu)q$, and define the full static energy
$$\mathcal E_L(\mathcal A,q)=\int_0^L\!\int_{\mathbb R^2}\left[\frac{B_{12}^2+F_{31}^2+F_{32}^2}{2e^2}+|D_1q|^2+|D_2q|^2+|D_3q|^2+\frac{e^2}{2}(|q|^2-\xi)^2\right]dx_1dx_2dz,$$
where $B_{12}=F_{12}$. Call such a pair admissible of winding $n$ if its energy is finite, every transverse slice has finite $E_\perp$, and there are $R_0>0$ and smooth $\rho>0$ and real $2\pi$-periodic $\phi$ on $\{|x|>R_0\}\times[0,L]$ such that $q=\rho e^{i(n\theta+\phi)}$, with $\rho\to\sqrt\xi$ and $\phi\to0$ uniformly in $z$ and $\theta$ as $|x|\to\infty$. Require that each slice has flux $\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_{D_R}B_{12}\,dx_1dx_2=2\pi n$, and require the angular one-form condition
$$\lim_{R\to\infty}\sup_{0\le z\le L}\left|\int_{\partial D_R}(A_1dx_1+A_2dx_2-n\,d\theta)\right|=0$$
and zero radial magnetic-flux leakage, meaning that the integral of $F$ over the side $\partial D_R\times[0,L]$ tends to zero as $R\to\infty$. The infimum below is over admissible pairs with fixed smooth finite-energy end traces $p_0=(A^0,q^0)$ and $p_1=(A^1,q^1)$ in winding $n$. If their exterior phase is $n\theta+\phi_j$, first apply the globally smooth degree-zero gauge cleanup proved below and prescribe the resulting representatives as the end values. The common canonical exterior gauge means $q^j=\rho_j e^{in\theta}$ and $A^j-n\,d\theta\in L^2$ outside a disk, with the angular one-form limit above.

For any two such fixed end traces, the cleaned differences $q^1-q^0$ and $A^1-A^0$ lie in $L^2(\mathbb R^2)$. Choose any finite collection of distinct points $z_j\in\mathbb C$ with positive integer multiplicities $m_j$ summing to $|n|$ (the empty collection for $n=0$), and let $p_*=(A^*,q^*)$ be its planar minimizing field pair in canonical exterior gauge. Set $T_n=2\pi\xi|n|$. There are a fixed collar width $\ell>0$ and finite constants $C_0,C_1$, depending on the end traces, $p_*$, and the chosen smooth collar profile but not on $L$, such that for every $L\ge2\ell$,
$$T_nL\le\inf\mathcal E_L\le T_n(L-2\ell)+C_0+C_1.$$
Consequently the difference $\inf\mathcal E_L-T_nL$ remains bounded as $L\to\infty$. If both fixed end traces are the same planar minimizing pair, its constant extension in $z$ attains the exact minimum $T_nL$. This is a mathematical fixed-flux boundary variational statement and does not assert a point-source self-energy or a quantum Wilson-loop result.

The gauge transformations used to put an end trace in canonical exterior gauge have the form $(q,A)\mapsto(e^{i\chi}q,A+d\chi)$ for a smooth real-valued function $\chi$ on the whole plane; the function is globally defined by extending a radial cutoff times the single-valued periodic phase correction.

manifest_declaration.title: A double vortex and a separate third vortex
manifest_declaration.statement:
Let $e,\xi>0$, $\kappa=2e^2\xi$, and let $z_0\ne z_1$ be any two points of $\mathbb C$. For the positive-winding divisor $D=2[z_0]+[z_1]$, whose degree is $3$, the unique scalar solution satisfies
$$\Delta h+\kappa(1-e^h)=8\pi\delta_{z_0}+4\pi\delta_{z_1},\qquad h-4\log|z-z_0|\text{ extends smoothly at }z_0,\qquad h-2\log|z-z_1|\text{ extends smoothly at }z_1,\qquad h\to0\text{ at infinity},$$
with $h<0$ off $\{z_0,z_1\}$. For $P(z)=(z-z_0)^2(z-z_1)$ and $s=2\log|P|$, the reconstructed fields $q=\sqrt\xi e^{(h-s)/2}P$ and $A=-\tfrac12*d(h-s)$ are smooth, have flux $6\pi$, and attain transverse energy $6\pi\xi$. The solution is specified by this unique nonlinear elliptic problem; no elementary closed-form profile is asserted.

Separately, for each $n\in\mathbb Z$ and each effective divisor of degree $|n|$, the corresponding planar minimizer has signed flux $2\pi n$ and transverse energy $T_n=2\pi\xi|n|$. For fixed smooth end traces in winding $n$ and the same canonical exterior gauge, its cylinder infimum satisfies
$$T_nL\le\inf\mathcal E_L\le T_n(L-2\ell)+C_0+C_1\quad(L\ge2\ell),$$
for a fixed collar width $\ell>0$ and finite constants $C_0,C_1$ independent of $L$; matching minimizing end traces give the exact value $T_nL$. This is the fixed-flux variational estimate for the stated cylinder class.

manifest_declaration.title: Why a nonproper fixed locus needs another theory
manifest_declaration.statement: Let $T=\mathbb C^\times$ act trivially on $X=\mathbb C^\times=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C[z,z^{-1}]$. Then the fixed locus is $F=X$, and $F\to\mathrm{pt}$ is not proper. Here proper means finite-type, separated, and universally closed; after base change to $\mathbb A^1$ with coordinate $s$, the closed subset $\{(z,s):zs=1\}\subseteq\mathbb C^\times\times\mathbb A^1$ projects to the nonclosed subset $\mathbb A^1\setminus\{0\}$. Consequently the intrinsic localized pushforward defined using a proper fixed-locus trace has no value on $[F]_T$; this example assigns no fixed-point integral or reciprocal-Euler sum.

manifest_declaration.title: Local transforms versus global injectivity
manifest_declaration.design_state: Authored in batch 68; no design section governs this pair.
manifest_declaration.statement: Let $U_N$ and $U_S$ be the two stereographic charts of $S^4$, and let $\xi\in H^1(Z,F\otimes\mathcal O_Z(-2))$ be a global class under the coupled theorem's hypotheses. On each chart compute the fibre-harmonic section from a global closed Dolbeault representative. On $U_N\cap U_S$ the two local sections agree because they are the harmonic projection on the same fibre and are unchanged by replacing the representative by a Dolbeault-exact form. If the glued section is zero, the global class is zero by injectivity. Thus a local contour expression alone establishes neither compatibility on the overlap nor injectivity of the global class map.

manifest_declaration.title: A positive-FI point with a non-locally-free framed sheaf
manifest_declaration.statement:
Take $N=k=1$ and $\zeta>0$. The datum $B_1=B_2=0$, $I=\sqrt\zeta$, $J=0$ is a stable positive-FI solution but is not costable and does not lie in the zero-FI regular locus. Its stable complex orbit has the framed $\mathbb P^2$ monad

$$\mathcal O(-1)\xrightarrow{(-z_1,-z_2,0)^T}\mathcal O^{\oplus3}\xrightarrow{(z_2,-z_1,z_0)}\mathcal O(1),$$

whose middle cohomology is the ideal sheaf of $p=[1:0:0]$; it is torsion-free and not locally free at $p$. Thus this positive-FI point lies on the non-locally-free boundary excluded from the ordinary zero-FI framed ASD correspondence.

manifest_declaration.title: An exact raw one-instanton block
manifest_declaration.statement:
Let $V=\mathbb C$, $W=\mathbb C^2$ with their standard Hermitian forms, and
let $\rho>0$. Take
$$
B_1=B_2=0,\qquad I=(\rho,0):W\to V,\qquad
J=(0,\rho)^T:V\to W.
$$
Both ADHM moments vanish. The associated homogeneous monad maps on
$\mathbb P^3$ are
$$
\alpha=
\begin{pmatrix}
-\mu_1\\-\mu_2\\\rho\lambda_2\\\rho\lambda_1
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\beta=(\mu_2,-\mu_1,\rho\lambda_1,-\rho\lambda_2).
$$
For $z=(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2$, put
$$
D_z=
\begin{pmatrix}
z_2&-z_1&\rho&0\\
-\bar z_1&-\bar z_2&0&\rho
\end{pmatrix},\qquad
f_z=|z_1|^2+|z_2|^2+\rho^2.
$$
Then $D_zD_z^\dagger=f_z I_2$. The orthogonal projection
$P_z=I_4-D_z^\dagger f_z^{-1}D_z$ has image $\ker D_z$, a rank-two Hermitian
bundle over $\mathbb R^4$. Its projection connection is $\nabla=P\,d$.
With $z_1=x^0+ix^1$, $z_2=x^2+ix^3$, and positive orientation
$dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, its curvature satisfies
$F^+=\tfrac12(F+*F)=0$. The monad is trivial and positive on every real
line, and its infinity framing is the identity framing by $W$.

references.title: Simon K. Donaldson, The ADHM construction of Yang–Mills instantons

manifest_declaration.title: Zero-charge positive real monad
manifest_declaration.statement:
Let $N\ge2$, $k=0$, $V=\mathbb C^0$, and let $W=\mathbb C^N$ with its standard
Hermitian form and fixed unitary framing. The unique maps
$B_1,B_2\in\operatorname{End}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, and $J:V\to W$ are zero.
Their ADHM moments vanish, the stability and costability conditions are
vacuous, and the raw monad is
$$
0\longrightarrow W\otimes\mathcal O
\longrightarrow 0.
$$
Its middle cohomology is the framed trivial bundle $W\otimes\mathcal O$,
positive on every real-line section space. The normalized gauge group
$U(0)$ has one element, so no gauge or normal-form parameters remain. Its
algebraic and topological second Chern classes vanish and its Euler
characteristic is $N$.

manifest_declaration.title: Compactness of the finite complex Grassmannian
manifest_declaration.design_state: Step 1 argument and contract are complete; current native readiness record is ready.
manifest_declaration.statement: Let $N\ge2$. For $1\le k<N$, let $\operatorname{Gr}_{\mathbb C}(k,N)$ be the set of matrices $P\in M_N(\mathbb C)$ satisfying $P^*=P$, $P^2=P$, and $\operatorname{tr}P=k$, with the topology inherited from $M_N(\mathbb C)\cong\mathbb R^{2N^2}$. The map $P\mapsto\operatorname{ran}P$ identifies this space with the usual Grassmannian of complex $k$-planes in $\mathbb C^N$. The finite union $\mathscr G_N=\bigcup_{1\le k<N}\operatorname{Gr}_{\mathbb C}(k,N)$ is compact.

manifest_declaration.title: Dimension of the finite holonomy incidence manifold
manifest_declaration.design_state: Step 1 argument and contract are complete; current native readiness record is ready.
manifest_declaration.statement:
Let $N\ge2$, $r\ge1$, and $1\le k<N$. For each orthogonal projection $P$ onto a complex $k$-plane in $\mathbb C^N$, write $V_P=\operatorname{ran}P$. Define
$$
I_{k,r}=\{(g_1,\ldots,g_r,P)\in SU(N)^r\times\operatorname{Gr}_{\mathbb C}(k,N):g_iV_P=V_P\text{ for every }i\},
$$
where $SU(N)$ has its usual matrix Lie-group structure and $\operatorname{Gr}_{\mathbb C}(k,N)$ has the orthogonal-projection topology. Then $I_{k,r}$ is a closed embedded smooth submanifold,
$$
\dim I_{k,r}=2k(N-k)+r\bigl(k^2+(N-k)^2-1\bigr).
$$
Its codimension in $SU(N)^r\times\operatorname{Gr}_{\mathbb C}(k,N)$ is $2r\,k(N-k)$, and
$$
\dim SU(N)^r-\dim I_{k,r}=2(r-1)k(N-k).
$$

manifest_declaration.title: Finite holonomy witnesses for irreducibility
manifest_declaration.design_state: Step 1 argument and contract are complete; current direct and transitive inputs have ready records. This does not claim independent proof approval.
manifest_declaration.statement: Assume ZF together with the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be $S^3$ or $S^4$ with its compact, connected, oriented, boundaryless smooth structure and a smooth Riemannian metric. Let $N\ge2$, let $P\to M$ be a smooth principal right $SU(N)$-bundle, choose a smooth reference connection $A_0$, a basepoint $m\in M$, and a frame of the fiber $P_m$. Put $\mathcal A_\infty=A_0+\Omega^1(M;\operatorname{ad}P)$ with its $C^\infty$ section topology. For a smooth connection $A$, let $\operatorname{Hol}_A\subseteq SU(N)$ be the group generated by parallel transports along based piecewise-smooth loops at $m$, expressed in the chosen frame. Call $A$ irreducible when the standard action of $\operatorname{Hol}_A$ on $\mathbb C^N$ has no nonzero proper invariant complex subspace, and write $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ for this locus. For each integer $q>\dim(M)/2+1$, let $\mathcal G_{q+1}$ be the $H^{q+1}$ gauge group of sections of $\operatorname{Ad}P$, acting on $H^q$ connections by the local formula $A^u=u^{-1}Au+u^{-1}du$, and let $Z_N=\{\zeta I_N:\zeta^N=1\}$. Measure $C^1$ closeness by coefficient and first-derivative suprema in a fixed finite bundle atlas. For every $A\in\mathcal A_\infty^*$, a finite tuple of based piecewise-smooth loops has holonomies with no common nonzero proper invariant subspace; the same tuple continues to witness irreducibility on a $C^1$ neighborhood of $A$, so $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ is open in the $C^\infty$ topology. The stabilizer of $A$ in $\mathcal G_{q+1}$ is exactly $Z_N$. Irreducibility here does not assert $\operatorname{Hol}_A=SU(N)$.

manifest_declaration.title: Relative finite-parameter avoidance of reducible connections
manifest_declaration.design_state: Step 1 argument and contract are complete; current direct and transitive inputs have ready records. This does not claim independent proof approval.
manifest_declaration.statement: Assume ZF together with the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be $S^3$ or $S^4$ with its compact, connected, oriented, boundaryless smooth structure, let $N\ge2$, and let $P\to M$ be a smooth principal right $SU(N)$-bundle with a smooth reference connection $A_0$. Fix a basepoint $m\in M$ and a frame of $P_m$. Equip $\mathcal A_\infty=A_0+\Omega^1(M;\operatorname{ad}P)$ with the Fréchet topology generated by suprema of all derivatives of section coefficients in a fixed finite bundle atlas. Let $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ consist of connections whose based holonomy action on $\mathbb C^N$ has no nonzero proper invariant complex subspace. Let $K$ be the geometric realization of a finite simplicial complex, let $L$ be the realization of a subcomplex, and let $f:K\to\mathcal A_\infty$ be continuous with $f(L)\subseteq\mathcal A_\infty^*$. Then there is a continuous homotopy $H:K\times[0,1]\to\mathcal A_\infty$, fixed on $L$ and on an open neighborhood of $L$, such that $H(\cdot,1)$ maps all of $K$ into $\mathcal A_\infty^*$. For every finite list of these $C^\infty$ section seminorms $p_1,\ldots,p_m$ and positive tolerances $\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_m$, the homotopy can be chosen with $\sup_{(s,t)\in K\times[0,1]}p_j(H(s,t)-f(s))<\epsilon_j$ for every $j$.

manifest_declaration.title: Weak contractibility of the irreducible connection locus
manifest_declaration.design_state: Step 1 argument and contract are complete; current direct and transitive inputs have ready records. This does not claim independent proof approval.
manifest_declaration.statement: Assume ZF together with the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be $S^3$ or $S^4$, let $N\ge2$, and let $P\to M$ be any smooth principal right $SU(N)$-bundle. Fix a smooth reference connection $A_0$, a basepoint $m\in M$, and a frame of $P_m$. Equip the affine space $\mathcal A_\infty=A_0+\Omega^1(M;\operatorname{ad}P)$ with its $C^\infty$ section topology, and let $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ be the connections whose based holonomy action on $\mathbb C^N$ has no nonzero proper invariant complex subspace. Then $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ is nonempty and path-connected, and for every $A\in\mathcal A_\infty^*$ and every integer $j\ge1$, $\pi_j(\mathcal A_\infty^*,A)=0$. Here $\pi_j(X,x)$ is the based homotopy group of continuous maps $u:(I^j,\partial I^j)\to(X,x)$ modulo homotopies that keep $\partial I^j$ at $x$.

manifest_declaration.design_state: Step 1 argument and contract are complete; current direct and transitive inputs have ready records. This does not claim independent proof approval.
manifest_declaration.statement: Assume ZF together with the Axiom of Choice. Let $M=S^3$ or $S^4$, let $N\ge2$, take the trivial principal right $SU(N)$-bundle $P=M\times SU(N)$, and use its zero connection as affine origin. For any integer $j\ge1$ and any continuous sphere family $f:S^j\to\mathcal A_\infty^*$ of smooth connections on $P$, the cone formula $F([r,x])=r f(x)$ extends $f$ continuously over $D^{j+1}$ in the full affine connection space. The apex is the zero connection, whose holonomy group is the identity and which preserves every complex line, so this affine filling is reducible and does not lie entirely in $\mathcal A_\infty^*$. Relative avoidance changes the filling while fixing its boundary and produces a filling in $\mathcal A_\infty^*$; contraction of the disk to any chosen boundary point gives a based nullhomotopy. The weak-contractibility theorem ensures that such families exist for the trivial bundle and that their based homotopy classes vanish.

manifest_declaration.title: Adopted ABJM localization model on the round three-sphere
manifest_declaration.design_state: A-page adopted source-specific ABJM N=2 model on round S3, with exact global form, levels, field content, R-charges, zero deformations, contour, gauge fixing, and formal measure limit.
manifest_declaration.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Fix $r>0$ with units of length and the round oriented sphere
$$
\mathbb S^3_r=\{y\in\mathbb R^4:\textstyle\sum_{\alpha=1}^4 y_\alpha^2=r^2\}
$$
with its induced Riemannian metric, no boundary, and its unique spin structure. Adopt the source-specific ABJM model on this background, viewed through one chosen three-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ subalgebra. Its gauge group is $G=U(N)\times U(N)$ with $N\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}$ and supersymmetric Chern–Simons levels $k$ and $-k$, where $k\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$. The global group includes both central $U(1)$ factors. Write $\operatorname{tr}_N$ for the trace in the defining representation of either factor; in the Kapustin–Willett–Yaakov convention the level multiplies $\operatorname{tr}_N/(4\pi)$ in the supersymmetric Chern–Simons action.

Each $\mathcal N=2$ vector multiplet has a Hermitian matrix-valued connection $A_\mu$ (or $\widehat A_\mu$), a real Hermitian adjoint scalar $\sigma$ (or $\widehat\sigma$), a two-component complex gaugino $\lambda$ (or $\widehat\lambda$), and a real auxiliary scalar $D$ (or $\widehat D$). In an oriented coordinate chart the first factor's source-normalized action is
$$
S_{\mathrm{CS},k}=\frac{k}{4\pi}\int d^3x\,\operatorname{tr}_N\!\left(\epsilon^{\mu\nu\rho}\left(A_\mu\partial_\nu A_\rho+\frac{2i}{3}A_\mu A_\nu A_\rho\right)-\lambda^\dagger\lambda+2D\sigma\right);
$$
the second factor uses the same expression with $(A,\lambda,D,\sigma,k)$ replaced by $(\widehat A,\widehat\lambda,\widehat D,\widehat\sigma,-k)$. Here $\epsilon^{\mu\nu\rho}$ is the oriented Levi-Civita density.

The matter consists of two chiral multiplets $A_a$, $a=1,2$, in $(\mathbf N,\overline{\mathbf N})$ and two $B_{\dot a}$, $\dot a=1,2$, in $(\overline{\mathbf N},\mathbf N)$. A chiral multiplet means a complex scalar, a two-component complex spinor, and a complex auxiliary scalar in its stated representation. For $A_a$, for example, a gauge transformation $(U,\widehat U)\in G$ acts by $A_a\mapsto U A_a\widehat U^{-1}$; the $B_{\dot a}$ action is the reversed one. The covariant derivative on a bifundamental scalar is $D_\mu A_a=\partial_\mu A_a+iA_\mu A_a-iA_a\widehat A_\mu$; spinors also carry the Levi-Civita spin connection. The vector-multiplet fields act in that representation by left multiplication from the first factor minus right multiplication from the second.

The round-sphere component action for one chiral multiplet $(\phi,\psi,F)$ of $R$-charge $\Delta=\tfrac12$, in the representation determined by its bifundamental type, is
$$
S_{\mathrm{chiral}}=\int_{\mathbb S^3_r}d^3x\,\sqrt g\left((D_\mu\phi)^\dagger D^\mu\phi+\frac{3}{4r^2}\phi^\dagger\phi+i\psi^\dagger\gamma^\mu D_\mu\psi+F^\dagger F-\phi^\dagger\sigma^2\phi+\phi^\dagger D\phi-\psi^\dagger\sigma\psi+i\phi^\dagger\lambda^\dagger\psi-i\psi^\dagger\lambda\phi\right).
$$
The representation-valued $\sigma,D,\lambda$ in this expression act by the first-factor action minus the second-factor action. Sum this action over the four chiral multiplets.

The adopted $\mathcal N=2$ superpotential is
$$
W=\frac{2\pi}{k}\epsilon^{ab}\epsilon^{\dot a\dot b}\operatorname{tr}_N(A_aB_{\dot a}A_bB_{\dot b})=\frac{4\pi}{k}\operatorname{tr}_N(A_1B_1A_2B_2-A_1B_2A_2B_1),
$$
where $\epsilon^{12}=1=-\epsilon^{21}$ and all other components vanish. The superpotential is the holomorphic interaction that supplies the chiral auxiliary-field and Yukawa terms. This is the ABJM quartic interaction; the adopted quantum model has the enhanced $\mathcal N=6$ superconformal symmetry, while localization uses only the selected $\mathcal N=2$ subalgebra. The scalar component of each chiral multiplet has $U(1)_R$ charge and superconformal dimension $\Delta=\tfrac12$; its fermion and auxiliary component have charges $\Delta-1$ and $\Delta-2$. Set all real masses and Fayet–Iliopoulos parameters to zero. A real mass here is the constant scalar in a background flavor vector multiplet; a Fayet–Iliopoulos parameter is the coefficient of the auxiliary $D$ field for an abelian vector multiplet. The level $k$ is dimensionless, $r$ has units of length, $[A_\mu]=[\sigma]=[\lambda]=r^{-1}$, $[D]=r^{-2}$, $[\phi]=r^{-1/2}$, $[\psi]=r^{-1}$, and $[F]=r^{-3/2}$.

The smooth field domain consists of pairs of smooth connections and the listed smooth associated matter and auxiliary fields on the trivial $U(N)\times U(N)$ bundles. The smooth gauge group $C^\infty(\mathbb S^3_r,U(N)\times U(N))$ acts by the transformations just specified. The source gauge-fixes this quotient by the covariant Lorenz conditions $\nabla^\mu A_\mu=\nabla^\mu\widehat A_\mu=0$. Its Faddeev–Popov ghosts are anticommuting scalar fields representing the determinant of the derivative of these gauge conditions along gauge orbits. The Euclidean contour takes the vector connections and real scalars on their Hermitian/real slices, pairs each matter scalar with its Hermitian conjugate, and integrates the fermions as independent Grassmann variables. The diagonal Hermitian matrices form the Cartan subalgebras; the residual Weyl group $S_N\times S_N$, with $S_N$ the permutation group on $N$ entries, permutes their eigenvalues. The Cartan eigenvalues lie on real lines.

Choose a normalized conformal Killing spinor $\epsilon$ satisfying $\nabla_\mu\epsilon=\frac{i}{2r}\gamma_\mu\epsilon$ in an orthonormal frame, where $\gamma_\mu$ are Hermitian two-dimensional gamma matrices. Let $Q$ be its off-shell supersymmetry transformation and let $\delta_{\mathrm{FP}}$ be the Faddeev–Popov differential. In the source gauge-fixed complex, $Q_{\mathrm{gf}}=Q+\delta_{\mathrm{FP}}$ is odd and squares to zero on the gauge-fixed fields and ghosts. The source localization calculation adds a dimensionless parameter $t$ times a $Q_{\mathrm{gf}}$-exact Yang–Mills deformation. Its one-loop determinants are zeta-regularized, with $\log\det L=-\zeta_L'(0)$ when the source's spectral hypotheses apply; they are the Gaussian boson/fermion/ghost determinant ratios about the constant-Cartan locus.

The corresponding gauge-fixed functional integral is only the formal expression
$$
Z_{\mathrm{formal}}=\frac{1}{\operatorname{vol}(\mathcal G)}\int_{\mathcal C/\mathcal G}[D\Phi]\,e^{-S_E[\Phi]},
$$
where $\mathcal G=C^\infty(\mathbb S^3_r,U(N)\times U(N))$, $\mathcal C$ is the source Euclidean contour, and $S_E$ is the supersymmetric Chern–Simons, chiral-matter, and superpotential action specified above. The source calculation assumes that its gauge-fixed measure and contour are $Q_{\mathrm{gf}}$-invariant and that the deformation introduces no anomalous Jacobian (a multiplicative change of the formal measure under $Q_{\mathrm{gf}}$) or surface contribution at the boundary of field space. These are adopted formal field-theory inputs: this postulate does not construct an infinite-dimensional measure, prove convergence of the localization limit, or assert a theorem for arbitrary three-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ models.

manifest_declaration.statement:
Fix the adopted zero-mass, zero-Fayet–Iliopoulos ABJM model on the round sphere of radius $r>0$, with $N\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}$ and nonzero integer level $k$. Let $s_i,\widehat s_i\in\mathbb R$ be the eigenvalues of the two constant Hermitian Cartan scalars, each of physical dimension $r^{-1}$, and put $\lambda_i=rs_i$ and $\widehat\lambda_i=r\widehat s_i$. In the Kapustin–Willett–Yaakov Euclidean level convention, the source-reported formal localization expression is
$$
Z_{\mathrm{ABJM}}(\mathbb S^3_r)=\frac{1}{(N!)^2}\int_{\mathbb R^{2N}}\left(\prod_{i=1}^N d\lambda_i\,d\widehat\lambda_i\right)e^{-i\pi k\left(\sum_i\lambda_i^2-\sum_i\widehat\lambda_i^2\right)}\frac{\displaystyle\prod_{1\le i<j\le N}\left(2\sinh\!\left(\pi(\lambda_i-\lambda_j)\right)\right)^2\left(2\sinh\!\left(\pi(\widehat\lambda_i-\widehat\lambda_j)\right)\right)^2}{\displaystyle\prod_{i,j=1}^N\left(2\cosh\!\left(\pi(\lambda_i-\widehat\lambda_j)\right)\right)^2}.
$$
Each Cartan variable is integrated over the real line. The integer level and the dimensionless eigenvalues fix every exponent and hyperbolic-function argument; the factor $(N!)^{-2}$ is the inverse order of the two Weyl groups. Mariño's convention uses $\mu_i=2\pi\lambda_i$ and $g_s=2\pi i/k_{\mathrm{Marino}}$; it gives the same displayed phase after setting $k_{\mathrm{Marino}}=-k$. The displayed real-contour expression is oscillatory. It is the source's matrix-integral result under its formal localization and determinant prescriptions, not a construction of the continuum functional measure, a proof of the localization limit, or a formula for every three-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ theory.

manifest_declaration.statement:
Use the adopted round-$S^4_r$ $\mathcal N=2^*$ $U(2)$ model with one adjoint hypermultiplet of real Euclidean mass $m_E$, dimensionless coupling $g_{\mathrm{YM}}>0$, theta angle $\theta$, and natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Thus $[r]=\mathrm{mass}^{-1}$, while $m_E$, Cartan parameters, and $\epsilon_i$ have mass dimension one; $\tau=4\pi i/g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2+\theta/(2\pi)$ and $q=e^{2\pi i\tau}$ are dimensionless. Put

The source continues its algebraic mass as $m=i m_E$ for real Euclidean $m_E$. Put

$$\epsilon_1=\epsilon_2=\epsilon=r^{-1},\qquad \widetilde m=i m_E+\frac{\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2}{2}.$$

For the fixed-point algebra below, first treat $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2$ and the complexified Coulomb weights as generic equivariant variables. Sum the fixed-point terms as a rational function before imposing the round-sphere values; on the physical contour the source uses $\epsilon_1=\epsilon_2=r^{-1}$ and imaginary Nekrasov Coulomb weights. 

For $U(2)$ the nonzero roots are $\pm\alpha_{12}$, and the Weyl group is $S_2$. Use Pestun's full Lie-algebra integral convention $a\in\mathfrak u(2)$, $(a,a)=-\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf 2}(a^2)$, measure $[da]$, and gauge-volume factor $\operatorname{vol}(U(2))$. Its Cartan rewrite uses the source's Weyl factor $\Delta(a)=\prod_{\alpha\in\mathrm{Roots}(U(2))}\alpha\cdot a$. The $\mathfrak u(2)$ expression below is the displayed convention, so no separate $1/|S_2|$ is inserted there. 

Write the real Cartan integration parameters in the source convention as $a_E=(a_1^E,a_2^E)$. The one-loop determinant is evaluated at the analytically continued argument $ia_E$, while the Nekrasov factor uses complexified Coulomb weights $a_\alpha^{\mathrm P}=i a_\alpha^E$, as in the source's continuation. Thus $\alpha_{12}(a_E)=a_1^E-a_2^E$ in the one-loop product and $\alpha_{12}(a^{\mathrm P})=i(a_1^E-a_2^E)$ in the instanton series. 

The source's regularized one-loop factor is

$$Z_{1\text{-loop}}^{\mathcal N=2^*}(i a_E;m_E)= \prod_{\alpha\in\mathrm{Roots}(U(2))}\prod_{n=1}^{\infty} \left[\frac{((\alpha\cdot a_E)^2+\epsilon^2n^2)^2} {((\alpha\cdot a_E+m_E)^2+\epsilon^2n^2) ((\alpha\cdot a_E-m_E)^2+\epsilon^2n^2)}\right]^{n/2}.$$

It is regularized by the source's Barnes-$G$ prescription after dropping the $a_E$-independent divergent factor. If the integral is rewritten on a Cartan, the Weyl factor is included once, separately from this root product. 

For a partition $Y$, use a finite downward-closed subset of $\mathbb Z_{\geq0}^2$ and write $|Y|$ for its box count. The source labels its boxes from $1$; translate $(i,j)$ to $(i-1,j-1)$ for the ADHM theorem, which does not change arm or leg lengths. If $s=(i,j)$ in the source's convention, let $\nu_i(Y)$ be the height of column $i$ and $\nu'_j(Y)$ the length of row $j$, and define $v_Y(s)=\nu_i(Y)-j$ and $h_Y(s)=\nu'_j(Y)-i$; these relative vertical and horizontal lengths may be negative when $s$ is outside $Y$. Let $\vec Y=(Y_1,Y_2)$, $|\vec Y|=|Y_1|+|Y_2|$, and let $a_\alpha^{\mathrm A}=c_1^T(e_\alpha)$ be the additive dual-framing weights in the ADHM convention. Let $a_\alpha^{\mathrm P}$ be Pestun's Coulomb weights in the Nekrasov factor. 

The exact convention match used here is $a_\alpha^{\mathrm A}=-a_\alpha^{\mathrm P}$: the ADHM framing representation has character $W=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$, whereas Pestun's Cartan element acts in the fundamental representation. 

In the source convention define

$$E_{\alpha\beta}(s)=-h_{Y_\beta}(s)\epsilon_1+(v_{Y_\alpha}(s)+1)\epsilon_2+a_\beta^{\mathrm P}-a_\alpha^{\mathrm P}.$$

The source's formal N=2* instanton factor is

$$Z_{\mathrm{inst}}^{\mathcal N=2^*}(a_1^{\mathrm P},a_2^{\mathrm P},\widetilde m;\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2,q)= \sum_{\vec Y}q^{|\vec Y|} \prod_{\alpha,\beta=1}^{2}\prod_{s\in Y_\alpha} \frac{(E_{\alpha\beta}(s)-\widetilde m) (\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2-E_{\alpha\beta}(s)-\widetilde m)} {E_{\alpha\beta}(s)(\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2-E_{\alpha\beta}(s))}.$$

Pestun reports the following formal partition-function expression:

$$Z_{S^4}^{\mathrm{formal}}= \frac{1}{\operatorname{vol}(U(2))}\int_{\mathfrak u(2)}[da]\, \exp\!\left[-\frac{8\pi^2r^2}{g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2}(a,a)\right] Z_{1\text{-loop}}^{\mathcal N=2^*}(ia;m_E) \left|Z_{\mathrm{inst}}^{\mathcal N=2^*} (ia,\widetilde m;\epsilon_1=r^{-1},\epsilon_2=r^{-1},q)\right|^2.$$

The absolute square denotes the north-pole instanton factor times the south-pole anti-instanton factor on the physical real slice; after complex continuation the two factors are kept independent. 

The charge-one coefficient of the mathematical ADHM localized Euler series is

$$C_1= \frac{(\epsilon_1-\widetilde m)(\epsilon_2-\widetilde m) (a_2^{\mathrm P}-a_1^{\mathrm P}+\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2-\widetilde m) (a_1^{\mathrm P}-a_2^{\mathrm P}-\widetilde m)} {\epsilon_1\epsilon_2(a_2^{\mathrm P}-a_1^{\mathrm P}+\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2) (a_1^{\mathrm P}-a_2^{\mathrm P})} + \frac{(a_1^{\mathrm P}-a_2^{\mathrm P}+\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2-\widetilde m) (a_2^{\mathrm P}-a_1^{\mathrm P}-\widetilde m) (\epsilon_1-\widetilde m)(\epsilon_2-\widetilde m)} {(a_1^{\mathrm P}-a_2^{\mathrm P}+\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2) (a_2^{\mathrm P}-a_1^{\mathrm P})\epsilon_1\epsilon_2}.$$

This is a source-reported structural prescription with a locally derived mathematical one-instanton coefficient, not a locally proved continuum path-integral identity.

The charge-one partition tuples are exactly $((\Box),\varnothing)$ and $(\varnothing,(\Box))$.

manifest_declaration.statement: Let $X$ be a compact finite-dimensional smooth manifold, $K\subseteq X$ a closed smooth submanifold with a chosen collar, $M$ a compact smooth manifold, and $E\to M$ a finite-rank smooth real vector bundle. Let $s:X\times M\to E$ be a continuous family of sections, meaning $s(x,m)\in E_m$ and $(x,m)\mapsto s(x,m)$ is continuous. Assume $x\mapsto s(x,\cdot)$ is continuous in the uniform topology, its restriction to $K$ is continuous in the $C^\infty$ section topology, and for distinct marked points $m_1,\ldots,m_q\in M$ the values $s(x,m_i)=v_i\in E_{m_i}$ are independent of $x$. For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a family $\widetilde s:X\to\Gamma^\infty(E)$ continuous in the $C^\infty$ topology, equal to $s$ on $K$, equal to $v_i$ at every $m_i$, and satisfying $\sup_{x,m}\|\widetilde s(x,m)-s(x,m)\|<\varepsilon$ for any fixed bundle norm. manifest_declaration.statement:
Let $P\to S^r$ be a smooth principal $SU(N)$ bundle with $r\in\{3,4\}$, $N\ge2$, a chosen point $m\in S^r$, and a chosen frame $p_m$ in its fiber. Write $\mathcal G(P):=\mathcal G_\infty(P)$ for the smooth gauge group defined by the finite-atlas $C^\infty$ section topology, let $\mathcal G_m(P):=\{u\in\mathcal G_\infty(P):u(p_m)=e\}$, and put $\overline{\mathcal G}(P):=\overline{\mathcal G}_\infty(P)=\mathcal G_\infty(P)/Z_N$, where $Z_N$ is the finite subgroup of constant central gauge sections. Evaluation $ev_m(u)=u(p_m)$ gives a locally trivial bundle
$$\mathcal G_m(P)\longrightarrow\mathcal G(P)\xrightarrow{ev_m}SU(N),$$
and the quotient map $\mathcal G(P)\to\overline{\mathcal G}(P)$ is a finite covering. For a local section $s:U\to\mathcal G(P)$, the bundle chart has the commutative form
$$\begin{array}{ccc}\mathcal G_m(P)\times U&\xrightarrow{\Phi_s}&ev_m^{-1}(U)\\\downarrow{\operatorname{pr}_2}&&\downarrow{ev_m}\\U&\hookrightarrow&SU(N)\end{array}$$
where $\Phi_s(v,g)=v\,s(g)$; the square commutes because $ev_m(v)=e$ and $ev_m(s(g))=g$. The corresponding TikZ source is:
```tikz
\begin{tikzcd}
\mathcal G_m(P)\times U \arrow[r,"\Phi_s"] \arrow[d,"\operatorname{pr}_2"'] & ev_m^{-1}(U) \arrow[d,"ev_m"]\\
U \arrow[r,hook] & SU(N)
\end{tikzcd}
```
The evaluation bundle is numerable; both maps are Serre fibrations and have the homotopy long exact sequence.

manifest_declaration.statement: Give $S^2\times S^2$ its product CW structure with $2$-skeleton $W=S^2\vee S^2$ and one oriented $4$-cell attached by $\alpha:S^3\to W$. Let $\nabla:W\to S^2$ fold the two oriented summands by the identity and put $\beta=\nabla\circ\alpha$. For a based map $f:S^3\to S^2$, its integral Hopf invariant $H(f)$ is defined by $x^2=H(f)y$ in the mapping cone $C_f=S^2\cup_fD^4$, where $x$ and $y$ are the positive generators of $H^2(C_f;\mathbb Z)$ and $H^4(C_f;\mathbb Z)$. With the product orientation, $H(\beta)=2$. Moreover the suspension $\Sigma\beta:S^4\to S^3$ is nullhomotopic. Consequently, if $\eta_3=\Sigma h$ is the suspension of the Hopf generator, then $2[\eta_3]=0$ in $\pi_4(S^3)$.

manifest_declaration.statement:
Adopt the following Euclidean source model in the conventions stated here. Let $r>0$ have units of length and let
$$S^4_r=\{y\in\mathbb R^5:\sum_{j=1}^5 y_j^2=r^2\}$$
have its round metric, standard orientation, and scalar curvature $12/r^2$. In stereographic coordinates $x^\mu$ of length, $\mu=1,\dots,4$, the metric is
$$ds^2=\frac{\sum_{\mu=1}^4(dx^\mu)^2}{(1+x^2/(4r^2))^2},\qquad x^2=\sum_{\mu=1}^4(x^\mu)^2.$$
Use the standard spin structure, a trivial $SU(2)_R$ background bundle with zero connection, and the $SU(2)_R$ generator selected below. The global gauge group is $G=SU(2)$, not $SO(3)$; its Lie algebra consists of anti-Hermitian $2\times2$ traceless matrices and has positive invariant form $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$, normalized by $\kappa(-i\sigma_a/2,-i\sigma_b/2)=\delta_{ab}$. Let $\Sigma$ be the declared set of isomorphism classes of smooth right principal $SU(2)$-bundles over $S^4_r$; each $P\in\Sigma$ is a separate gauge sector. The sector set and any sum over it are formal model inputs, not a classification or measure construction.

The matter content is the massless four-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ vector multiplet: one gauge connection $A_\mu$, six real adjoint scalar fields $\Phi_A$ with $A\in\{0,5,6,7,8,9\}$, and four adjoint Weyl fermions. Equivalently, its flat-space component content is one $\mathcal N=1$ vector multiplet and three adjoint $\mathcal N=1$ chiral multiplets. Set the topological $\theta$-term to zero in this selected model. Use the ordinary trace $\operatorname{Tr}_2$ in the defining representation of $SU(2)$ and a positive dimensionless coupling $g_{\mathrm{YM}}$. The current N=4 model carrier uses the same global group, $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$, the same dimensionless coupling, and connection-normalized adjoint chiral fields, with one vector and three adjoint chiral multiplets; this is an interface match for flat-space component content and normalization. This postulate separately adopts the source’s curved $S^4$ action, curvature coupling, selected-spinor algebra, gauge fixing, contour, and formal regulator inputs; it does not identify that curved action with the supplier’s flat Minkowski superspace action. For the dimensional-reduction notation, in a local gauge trivialization define the Lie-algebra-valued components $F_{\mu\nu}=\partial_\mu A_\nu-\partial_\nu A_\mu+[A_\mu,A_\nu]$, $F_{\mu A}=D_\mu\Phi_A$, and $F_{AB}=[\Phi_A,\Phi_B]$, extended antisymmetrically to $F_{MN}$. Here $D_\mu X=\nabla_\mu^{\mathrm{LC}}X+[A_\mu,X]$ on adjoint tensor fields, with the supplied spin connection on spinor indices, and $D_A X=[\Phi_A,X]$; in the fermion term $D_\mu\Psi$ includes the spin and gauge connections. These $F_{MN}$ are Lie-algebra-valued matrices, so $\operatorname{Tr}_2$ is taken in the defining representation. Use $\eta_{MN}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,\dots,1)$ for $M,N=0,\dots,9$. With the seven localization auxiliaries included, the adopted classical action input is
$$S_{\mathrm{off}}=-\frac{1}{g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2}\int_{S^4_r}d^4x\,\sqrt g\,\operatorname{Tr}_2\left(\frac12\sum_{M,N}F_{MN}F^{MN}-\Psi\Gamma^M D_M\Psi+\frac{2}{r^2}\sum_A\Phi_A\Phi^A-\sum_{i=1}^7K_iK_i\right).$$
Here $\Psi$ is the adjoint ten-dimensional Majorana–Weyl fermion used to package the four-dimensional fields; after Euclidean continuation it is complex and has no independent conjugate field. The chiral gamma matrices obey $\Gamma_M\widetilde\Gamma_N+\Gamma_N\widetilde\Gamma_M=2\eta_{MN}I_{16}$, with $\widetilde\Gamma_0=-\Gamma_0$ and $\widetilde\Gamma_M=\Gamma_M$ for $M=1,\dots,9$; $\Gamma_{MN}:=\widetilde\Gamma_{[M}\Gamma_{N]}$. The four sphere directions have positive metric. The term with $2/r^2$ is the conformal curvature coupling of the six scalars. The Yang–Mills coupling is dimensionless, $[A_\mu]=[\Phi_A]=\mathrm{length}^{-1}$, $[K_i]=[F_{MN}]=\mathrm{length}^{-2}$, and $[\Psi]=\mathrm{length}^{-3/2}$.

Let $\widehat\epsilon_s=(0_8,1,0_7)^{\mathsf T}$ be the normalized sixteen-component chiral spinor in the source gamma convention, with $\Gamma_{5678}\widehat\epsilon_s=\widehat\epsilon_s$ and $\Gamma_{1234}\widehat\epsilon_s=-\widehat\epsilon_s$, and set $\widehat\epsilon_c=(2r)^{-1}\Gamma_{012}\widehat\epsilon_s$. With $\Omega(x)=1+x^2/(4r^2)$, adopt
$$\epsilon(x)=\Omega(x)^{-1/2}\bigl(\widehat\epsilon_s+x^i\widetilde\Gamma_i\widehat\epsilon_c\bigr),\qquad \widetilde\epsilon(x)=\Omega(x)^{-1/2}\left(\widehat\epsilon_c-\frac{x^i}{4r^2}\Gamma_i\widehat\epsilon_s\right),\quad i=1,\dots,4.$$
They solve the conformal Killing-spinor system
$$\nabla_\mu\epsilon=\widetilde\Gamma_\mu\widetilde\epsilon,\qquad \nabla_\mu\widetilde\epsilon=-\frac{1}{4r^2}\Gamma_\mu\epsilon.$$
The selected spinors obey the source's same-chirality conditions, in particular $\widetilde\epsilon\epsilon=0$, so the dilation term in the supercharge square vanishes. Their bilinear $v^\mu=\epsilon\Gamma^\mu\epsilon$ generates the $U(1)$ isometry rotating the $(x^1,x^2)$ and $(x^3,x^4)$ planes equally. The corresponding internal R-symmetry generator is $R_{AB}=2\widetilde\epsilon\Gamma_{AB}\epsilon$ on scalar fields and its induced spin representation on fermions.

For this single supercharge, introduce seven adjoint auxiliary scalars $K_i$, $i=1,\dots,7$, and seven spinors $\nu_i$ satisfying
$$\epsilon\Gamma_M\nu_i=0,\qquad \frac12(\epsilon\Gamma^N\epsilon)\widetilde\Gamma_{N,\alpha\beta}=\sum_{i=1}^7\nu_{i,\alpha}\nu_{i,\beta}+\epsilon_\alpha\epsilon_\beta,\qquad \nu_i\Gamma_M\nu_j=\delta_{ij}\epsilon\Gamma_M\epsilon.$$
Adopt the off-shell transformations
$$Q_\epsilon A_M=\Psi\Gamma_M\epsilon,\qquad Q_\epsilon\Psi=\frac12\Gamma^{MN}F_{MN}\epsilon+\frac12\Gamma^\mu\Gamma^A\Phi_A\nabla_\mu\epsilon+\sum_iK_i\nu_i,\qquad Q_\epsilon K_i=-\nu_i\Gamma^M D_M\Psi.$$
With $v^M=\epsilon\Gamma^M\epsilon$, their square is the source's off-shell symmetry
$$Q_\epsilon^2=-\mathcal L_v-\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(v^M A_M)-\delta_R-\delta_\Omega,$$
where $\mathcal L_v$ is the lifted Lie derivative along the spacetime part $v^\mu$, $\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(u)$ acts on an adjoint field $X$ by $[u,X]$ and on a connection by $-D_\mu u$, $\delta_R$ is the internal transformation generated by $R_{AB}$, and $\delta_\Omega$ is the dilation with parameter $2\widetilde\epsilon\epsilon=0$. This off-shell closure is for the selected generator; it is not a claim that the full hypermultiplet algebra closes with finitely many auxiliary fields.

In a trivialization chart use the Faddeev–Popov gauge slice $d^*A=0$, where $d^*$ is the metric adjoint of the exterior derivative. In a nontrivial bundle sector $P$, choose a background connection $A_*$ and fluctuations $a=A-A_*$ in $\Omega^1(S^4,\operatorname{ad}P)$; the supplied local slice is $d_{A_*}^*a=0$ and its Faddeev–Popov operator is $d_{A_*}^*D_A$ with stabilizer modes omitted. Introduce odd ghost and antighost fields $c,\widetilde c$, an even multiplier $b$, and the constant zero-mode fields $a_0,\widetilde a_0,b_0,c_0,\widetilde c_0$. In the trivialization chart the Faddeev–Popov operator is $d^*D_{A_{\mathrm{gauge}}}$ with its zero modes omitted; its determinant is denoted $\det'(d^*D_{A_{\mathrm{gauge}}})$. Take dimensionless gauge-fixing parameters $\xi_1,\xi_2>0$ and the BRST gauge-fixing functional
$$\delta\left((\widetilde c,\,i d^*A+\tfrac{\xi_1}{2}b+i b_0)-(c,\,\widetilde a_0-\tfrac{\xi_2}{2}a_0)\right).$$
The brackets are the integrated invariant pairing on adjoint-valued fields, and the prime removes the stabilizer/constant zero modes treated by the displayed auxiliary fields. Let $S^\delta_{\mathrm{gf}}$ denote the BRST variation of this functional. If $\psi$ is the fermionic one-form superpartner of $A$ and $\rho_{\mathrm{gh}}(\omega)$ is the infinitesimal action of the selected circle generator on ghosts, the source's $Q$-closed completion is
$$S^Q_{\mathrm{gf}}=S^\delta_{\mathrm{gf}}-(\widetilde c,d^*\psi+\tfrac{\xi_1}{2}\rho_{\mathrm{gh}}(\omega)\widetilde c)-(\phi,\widetilde a_0-\tfrac{\xi_2}{2}a_0).$$
The gauge-fixed functional integral is the formal expression
$$Z_{\mathrm{formal}}=\sum_{[P]\in\Sigma}\frac{1}{\operatorname{vol}(\mathcal G(P),g_{\mathrm{YM}})} \int_{\mathcal C_P}[D\Phi\,Dc\,D\widetilde c\,Db\,D(\text{zero modes})]\, e^{-S_{\mathrm{off}}[P]-S_{\mathrm{gf}}^Q[P]}.$$
Here $\mathcal G(P)$ is the smooth gauge-automorphism group of $P$, $\mathcal C_P$ is the declared contour in that sector, and $\operatorname{vol}(\mathcal G(P),g_{\mathrm{YM}})$ is the source's formal gauge-group volume with its invariant measure scaled by the gauge coupling; it is not an actual infinite-dimensional Haar measure. In the Euclidean contour, gauge fields and $\Phi_{5},\dots,\Phi_9$ lie in the real Lie algebra, $\Phi_0=i\Phi_0^E$ with $\Phi_0^E$ real, the seven localization auxiliaries satisfy $K_i=iK_i^E$ with $K_i^E$ real, and $a_0=i a_0^E$ with $a_0^E$ real.

Let $\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(u)$ denote the infinitesimal gauge action with parameter $u$, and let $\delta_{U(1)}(\omega)$ denote the lifted infinitesimal circle action. The supersymmetry differential acts by $sX=X'$, $sX'=\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(\phi)X+\delta_{U(1)}(\omega)X$, $sc=\phi$, $s\phi=0$, $sa_0=0$, $s\widetilde c=s\widetilde a_0=sb_0=s\widetilde c_0=sc_0=0$, and $sb=\rho_{\mathrm{gh}}(\omega)\widetilde c$. The Faddeev–Popov differential acts on an adjoint-valued tensor field $X$ by $\delta X=-[c,X]$ and on its odd superpartner by $\delta X'=-[c,X']$. On the gauge connection it acts by $\delta A_\mu=D_\mu c=-\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(c)A_\mu$, using the earlier convention $\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(u)A_\mu=-D_\mu u$; the connection's one-form superpartner $\psi$ transforms as $\delta\psi=-[c,\psi]$. The remaining rules are $\delta c=-a_0-\tfrac12[c,c]$, $\delta a_0=0$, $\delta\phi=-[c,\phi]-\delta_{U(1)}(\omega)\phi$, $\delta\widetilde c=b$, $\delta b=[a_0,\widetilde c]$, $\delta\widetilde a_0=\widetilde c_0$, $\delta\widetilde c_0=[a_0,\widetilde a_0]$, $\delta b_0=c_0$, and $\delta c_0=[a_0,b_0]$. Here $X$ ranges over adjoint-valued physical and auxiliary tensor fields other than the connection, $X'$ is its odd superpartner, $c,\widetilde c,c_0,\widetilde c_0$ are odd, and $a_0,\widetilde a_0,b,b_0,\phi$ are even. The total localization differential is $Q=s+\delta$, with $s$ the supersymmetry differential and $\delta$ the Faddeev–Popov differential. These rules give, on adjoint-valued tensor fields and their superpartners,
$$s^2X'=\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(\phi)X'+\delta_{U(1)}(\omega)X',\qquad \delta^2X=\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(a_0)X,\qquad \{s,\delta\}X=-\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(\phi)X,$$
and the same graded algebra on the connection and its one-form superpartner when the gauge action on the connection is interpreted as $\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(u)A_\mu=-D_\mu u$. On ghosts, $\{s,\delta\}=\delta_{U(1)}(\omega)$ and $s^2=0$; the displayed ghost transformations give $\delta^2=\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(a_0)$. Thus $Q^2=\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(a_0)+\delta_{U(1)}(\omega)$ on fields and ghosts: a constant gauge transformation plus the $U(1)$ spacetime rotation. These are the finite-dimensional geometric symmetry data of the background; this assertion does not identify the infinite-dimensional field space with a smooth finite-dimensional manifold.

Adopt as a formal regulator the supersymmetry-compatible noncommutative deformation used by the source for gauge-field regularization on $\mathbb R^4$. Its $\Omega$-background is the $U(1)^2$ action rotating the two coordinate planes in $\mathbb R^4\cong\mathbb C^2$, with angular parameters $\varepsilon_1=\varepsilon_2=r^{-1}$, each of mass dimension one. For the four-sphere, assume an extension exists and agrees near the north and south poles with the stated $\mathbb R^4$ regulator. This extension is not explicitly constructed in the source and is an additional unresolved model assumption. The regulated measure, contour, and gauge-fixed action are likewise formal inputs; any use of $S_t=S+tQV$ is conditional on measure and contour invariance, no anomalous Jacobian, justified differentiation under the integral, and no uncontrolled boundary contribution. This postulate is a source-qualified modeling choice, not a proof of a continuum path integral or a result about nature.

manifest_declaration.statement: Take the adopted massless $\mathcal N=4$ model on the round $S^4_r$ with its specified conformal Killing spinors, seven auxiliary scalars, and combined gauge-fixed differential $Q=s+\delta$. For every adjoint-valued tensor field $X$ and its odd superpartner $X'$, the source algebra gives $sX=X'$, $sX'=\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(\phi)X+\delta_{U(1)}(\omega)X$, $\delta X=-[c,X]$, and $\delta X'=-[c,X']$, with $\delta^2X=\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(a_0)X$ and $\{s,\delta\}X=-\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(\phi)X$. On the ghost fields, $s^2=0$, $\delta^2=\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(a_0)$, and $\{s,\delta\}=\delta_{U(1)}(\omega)$. Thus the combined square is $Q^2=\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(a_0)+\delta_{U(1)}(\omega)$: a constant gauge transformation and the selected $U(1)$ isometry. The $U(1)$ factor acts smoothly on the finite-dimensional base $S^4_r$; its ordinary Cartan complex is the invariant polynomial-valued differential-form complex for that circle action. This finite Cartan complex concerns forms on $S^4_r$, not the infinite-dimensional field configuration space. The measure and noncommutative regulator extension remain formal assumptions of the adopted model.

source_metadata.title: ATLAS search for compressed higgsinos with low-momentum tracks
source_metadata.physical_scope: ATLAS Run-2 searches for electroweak higgsino-like states with compressed mass splittings, interpreted in the collaboration's stated simplified model. The reported selections, compatibility statements, and 95% confidence-level limits do not establish a supersymmetry-breaking vacuum or constrain spectra outside that model.

empirical_result.observation: The collaboration reports no significant excess in either the displaced-track or one-lepton-plus-one-track search. The observed displaced-track limit reaches about 200 GeV in chargino mass at a 0.6 GeV splitting; the one-lepton-plus-one-track limit reaches 130 GeV at a 2 GeV splitting. Combined, the searches exclude chargino masses below 126 GeV at 95% confidence level over the reported 0.3–2 GeV splitting range.
empirical_result.uncertainty: The integrated luminosity uncertainty is 0.83%. Statistical, detector, background, and signal-model uncertainties enter a profile-likelihood fit as Gaussian-constrained nuisance parameters with the correlations stated by the collaboration. The exclusion uses the asymptotic CLs procedure.
empirical_result.conditions: ATLAS 140 fb^-1 of proton-proton collisions at 13 TeV collected in 2015–2018; the displaced-track channel targets chargino-neutralino splittings about 0.3–1 GeV, while the one-lepton-plus-one-track channel targets about 1–3 GeV. The simplified higgsino model assumes the neutralino-2 to neutralino-1 mass splitting is twice the chargino-1 to neutralino-1 splitting.

empirical_result.observation: The collaboration reports no statistically significant overall deviation from the Standard Model in its global fit and quotes a 99% compatibility p-value for its specified test. It separately reports an electroweak direction pulled by the known A_FB^b and A_FB^c discrepancies. The quoted value is conditional on the collaboration's fit and calibration.
empirical_result.uncertainty: Input statistical, experimental-systematic, and theory uncertainties and their reported correlations enter the fit. The source's event-overlap treatment and input-specific uncertainty models are retained; raw events and component likelihoods are not independently reanalysed here.

source_metadata.title: ATLAS tau, jets, and missing-momentum squark and gluino search
source_metadata.physical_scope: ATLAS search for R-parity-conserving simplified squark and gluino models in tau, jets, and missing-transverse-momentum final states. The reported contours and local compatibility value apply only to the source's stated spectra, branching fractions, and analysis.

empirical_result.observation: The paper reports no significant overall deviation, a local p-value of 0.00058 (3.2 standard deviations) at its GG(1300,1200) benchmark, and observed 95% CLs exclusion contours reaching up to 2.25 TeV for gluinos in the machine-learning analysis and 2.3 TeV in the cut-and-count analysis, with squark reaches of 1.35 TeV and 1.7 TeV respectively. These values are model- and strategy-specific.
empirical_result.uncertainty: The analysis profiles source-correlated experimental and background nuisance parameters in a binned likelihood, validates its asymptotic approximation against simulation, and reports integrated-luminosity uncertainties of 0.83% for 13 TeV data and 2.0% for 13.6 TeV data. Theory cross-section uncertainty is shown as a variation of contours rather than profiled as an experimental nuisance in the fit.
empirical_result.conditions: ATLAS 140 fb^-1 at 13 TeV (2015–2018) plus 51.8 fb^-1 at 13.6 TeV (2022–2023), three orthogonal hadronic-tau/lepton channels, and the collaboration's R-parity-conserving simplified spectra with its stated intermediate-mass, branching-fraction, and narrow-width assumptions.

source_metadata.title: CMS search for supersymmetry with boosted hadronic and leptonic objects
source_metadata.physical_scope: Report of CMS-PAS-SUS-23-014, a Run-2 search for simplified supersymmetry models with boosted hadronic or leptonic objects. Its observed limits are conditional on the listed production and decay topologies and do not exclude supersymmetry as a framework.

empirical_result.observation: CMS reports no significant deviation from Standard Model expectations and model-specific 95% confidence-level cross-section limits. Representative observed mass reaches include gluinos up to 2.25 TeV (T5ttcc), 2.35 TeV (T5qqqqWH), and 2.30 TeV (T5bbbbZH); top squarks up to 1.45 TeV (T6ttZH); electroweakinos up to 1.05 TeV (TChiWZ) or 0.94 TeV (TChiWW); and the stated R-parity-violating bottom-squark and gluino reaches of 0.97 TeV (R2bbqqlv) and 1.82 TeV (R5ttbl).
empirical_result.uncertainty: The signal-region fit includes normalization and shape information and source-correlated nuisance parameters. Correction-factor background uncertainties range from 10–50%; boosted-object tagging uncertainties range from 5–15%, Higgs-tag uncertainties from 10–20% in the stated Higgs modes, and theory uncertainties from 5–30% depending on process. The CLs limits use the asymptotic approximation.
empirical_result.conditions: CMS 138 fb^-1 of pp collisions at 13 TeV collected in 2016–2018, with zero-lepton, isolated-lepton, or nonisolated-lepton channels selected by boosted-object categories and the MR and R^2 razor variables. Background correction factors are derived from control regions, applied to simulation, and checked in validation regions. Interpretations use the specific R-parity-conserving and R-parity-violating simplified models in the PAS.

manifest_declaration.title: Conditional Penrose vanishing from positive scalar curvature
manifest_declaration.statement:
Let $A$ be a smooth framed anti-self-dual unitary connection on the specified round oriented $S^4$, and let $\mathcal E$ be its holomorphic Ward bundle on $Z=\mathbb C\mathbb P^3$. Suppose the following conditional Penrose-transform input is supplied for both $\mathcal E$ and its dual $\mathcal E^\vee$: there are injective linear maps

$$\mathcal P_{\mathcal E}:H^1(Z,\mathcal E(-2))\longrightarrow\{s\in\Gamma(E):(\nabla_A^*\nabla_A+R/6)s=0\},$$

and the analogous map for $\mathcal E^\vee$, where $R>0$ is the scalar curvature of the round metric and the target connection is the induced unitary connection. Then

$$H^1(Z,\mathcal E(-2))=H^1(Z,\mathcal E^\vee(-2))=0.$$

This is a conditional vanishing result; it does not assert or prove the Penrose-transform input.

manifest_declaration.statement:
Let $p:E\to B$ be a nonempty locally trivial principal topological $H$-bundle with right $H$-action, and suppose it has a continuous section. For any $b_0\in B$, the fiber $H$ is a retract of $E$. If $E$ is weakly contractible, then $H$ is path connected and $\pi_j(H,e)=0$ for every $j\ge1$.

The retraction is expressed by the commutative diagram
$$\begin{array}{ccc}H&\xrightarrow{i}&E\\\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle\operatorname{id}_H}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle r}\\H&=&H\end{array}$$
with TikZ source
```tikz
\begin{tikzcd}
H \arrow[r,"i"] \arrow[dr,"\operatorname{id}_H"'] & E \arrow[d,"r"]\\
& H
\end{tikzcd}
```
